## Introduction

This purpose of this vignette is to demonstrate and document the complete
workflow for processing tree inventory data for the GEO-TREES initiative. The
code in this vignette matches the code in the R scripts elsewhere in this
repository. For automated processing of GEO-TREES tree inventory data it is
recommended to run the R scripts directly, not to use this vignette. This
vignette includes additional data visualisations to help understand how the
data is processed, and may provide a useful guide when processing a site for
the first time. Throughout the vignette there are sign-posts to the relevant R
script in the automated workflow.

Key steps of the workflow:

* Format raw field data to match the GEO-TREES L0 data format
* Align taxonomic names for each stem measurement
* Estimate height, wood density, and above-ground woody biomass of tree stems 
* Fit spatial polygons for each plot
* Calculate summary statistics of forest structure and biomass stocks within 50x50 m quadrats 


::: {#fig-flow fig-alt="GEO-TREES tree inventory processing workflow diagram." fig-align="center"}
![](img/tree_inv_geo-trees_flow.png)

Flow diagram of the GEO-TREES tree inventory processing workflow. Shaded boxes indicate core GEO-TREES data products (L1 = yellow, L2 = orange, L3 = green). Decisions on how data are analysed are taken at various stages of the processing chain: 1) stem height estimation, 2) wood density estimation, 3) stem AGB estimation, 4) stem filtering, 5) polygon fitting, 6) AGBD Monte-Carlo error propagation. Auxiliary field datasets can be included at multiple steps in this workflow, e.g.: local wood density, stem height measurements, crown dimensions (crown-distributed AGBD).
:::

This vignette uses an anonymised dataset, based on real data from a tropical
wet forest site in South America. To illustrate the use of all supported
auxiliary datasets and processing steps, some synthetic data have been
generated. 

Synthetic data are provided for:

* Locally-measured wood density estimates
* Locally-measured tree height estimates
* Local biomass and height allometries

## Setup

Required packages:

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: hide
library(dplyr)  # Dataframe manipulation
library(tidyr)  # Reshape dataframes, e.g. pivot_wider()
library(sf)  # Spatial data 
library(BIOMASS)  # AGB estimation, H:D allometry, 
library(yaml)  # read_yaml() - Read YAML files with parameters
library(ggplot2)  # Create plots and graphs
library(rocrateR)  # rocrate() etc. - Create RO-Crate meta-data files
library(kableExtra)  # Print dataframes in Quarto documents, only for the vignette
```

Source additional functions:

```{r}
source("../../func.R")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Functions provided in `func.R` and their descriptions."
# Extract function descriptions
kable(extractRoxygen("../../func.R"))
```

Set data input and output directories:

```{r}
indir <- "./data-raw/data"
outdir <- "./out"

# Directory for files to check raw data and the results of each step, and
# tables and figures for site reports, as in the automated workflow
report_dir <- file.path(outdir, "report")
```

## Create L0 data

This part of the workflow will vary among sites, depending on the structure of
the raw field data. Consult the [GEO-TREES Tree Inventory Data Collection
Guidelines](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Q5Wy_LbNEa0tNaGVntL0Bku41Z3t-TeU85_IxZuC6Uc/edit?usp=sharing)
Section 16: _Data format_ for information on the GEO-TREES L0 data format. [The
current repository](https://github.com/GEO-TREES/INV_processing) also contains
template files for formatting raw data, in the `./templates/` folder.

We provide various functions to help create valid GEO-TREES L0 data products:

* `pasteVals()` intelligently pastes values together, replacing NAs with blanks, useful for combining values in the `code` column.
* `colGen()` creates empty columns in a dataframe if they don't already exist, using a spec. table.
* `colCheck()` checks whether the columns in a dataframe exactly match those in a spec. table based on their name and class (e.g. numeric, character).
* `valCheck()` runs a series of simple logical checks on the different GEO-TREES Tree Inventory L0 data objects. 

You can see various examples of R scripts used to transform raw field data into
L0 data in `./sites/<SITE NAME>/<ACQUISITION ID>/01_fmt.R`.

::: {.callout-warning title="TODO"}
GEO-TREES also provides guidance on Quality Assurance and Quality Control of
tree inventory data.
:::

## Specify processing parameters

Choices made during the processing workflow, for example the choice to use a
local or regional height-diameter estimation method, should be specified in a
`param.yaml` YAML configuration file. This file also defines some site
meta-data and filepaths. 

There should be one `param.yaml` file for each version of the processed data.

`param.yaml` files should contain the following parameters:

* `site_id` -- Name of the site, e.g. `"Bicuar"`
* `acquisition_id` -- ID of data acquisition, e.g. `"2024"`
* `out_dir` -- Path to where processed data will be exported, e.g. `"./dat/sites/Bicuar/INV/2024/v1"`
* `raw_dir` -- Path to the raw input data, e.g. `"./dat/sites/Bicuar/INV/2024/L0"`
* `raw_version` -- Version of the raw input data, a sub-directory of `raw_dir`, e.g. `"v1"`. When raw data are corrected, create a new version so that previous outputs can still be reproduced
* `s3_dir` -- Optional, path to AWS S3 directory containing raw input data, e.g. `"johngodlee/GEO-TREES_INV/dat/sites/Amacayacu/INV/2024/L0"`
* `quad_dim` -- Dimensions in metres of quadrats, e.g. `[50, 50]` for 50x50 m square quadrats
* `opt_s3` -- Boolean (`true`/`false`). If `true`, raw input data will be pulled from an AWS S3 bucket specified in `s3_dir`, otherwise a local directory specified in `raw_dir`
* `product_version` -- String specifying the version of the data products, e.g. `"v1"`. Data products may be specified with different parameter sets, for example different size quadrats (`quad_dim`) or different methods of estimating stem height (`height_method`). 
* `software_version` -- String specifying the version of the code used to generate the data products, normally a GitHub release version, e.g. `"v2.4"`
* `height_method` -- Method used to estimate stem height: `"regional"` (Chave et al. 2014 Eq. 6a, with AGB from Eq. 7, which does not use height), `"field"` (a height-diameter model fitted to `height.csv`) or `"custom"` (a published height-diameter model given in `height_custom`). With `"field"` and `"custom"`, AGB is estimated with Chave et al. (2014) Eq. 4
* `wd_method` -- Method used to estimate wood density: `"regional"` (Global Wood Density Database v2), `"field"` (local measurements in `wd.csv`, replacing the Global Wood Density Database v2 estimates of the same taxa, with the Global Wood Density Database v2 for other taxa) or `"local"` (local measurements only, with genus, family and dataset means of the local species for taxa without a species estimate)
* `polygon_method` -- Method used to fit plot polygons, one of `"exact"`, `"affine"` or `"procrustes"`, see [Fit plot spatial polygons]
* `outside_max_dist_m` -- Maximum distance in metres outside the quadrat grid at which stems are assigned to the nearest quadrat, e.g. `5`. `0` excludes all stems outside the grid from quadrat summaries
* `corner_outlier_dist_m` -- Maximum distance in metres between a measured plot corner and the fitted plot polygon, beyond which the corner is treated as an outlier, e.g. `10`, see [Fit plot spatial polygons]
* `quad_grid_tol` -- Maximum proportion of the area of each plot which may be excluded from the grid of quadrats, e.g. `0.1`. The automated workflow centres the quadrat grid in each plot, so where the plot dimensions are not a multiple of the quadrat dimensions, equal strips along opposite edges of the plot are excluded, e.g. `0.4` allows 100 x 100 m quadrats in a 250 x 250 m plot, which excludes 36% of the plot
* `height_model` -- Height-diameter model used if `height_method` is `"field"`, one of `"best"` (lowest residual standard error), `"log1"`, `"log2"`, `"weibull"` or `"michaelis"`
* `agbd_diam_min_cm` -- Minimum stem diameter in cm for AGB density. The larger of this and the minimum diameter threshold of each plot is used, e.g. `0` uses the threshold of each plot
* `include_broken` -- `true` or `false`, whether stems broken above the POM are included in AGB density
* `multi_stem_method` -- How AGB is estimated for multi-stemmed trees, either `"equivalent"` (from the equivalent diameter of a single stem with the same basal area as the tree) or `"stem"` (from each stem separately)
* `unmapped_method` -- How trees without stem coordinates are treated, either `"random"` (assigned to a random quadrat in their plot in each Monte Carlo simulation) or `"exclude"` (excluded from AGB density)
* `diam_error` -- Diameter measurement error propagated to AGB, either `"chave2004"` (Chave et al. 2004), `"field"` (estimated from repeat diameter measurements in `stem_dup.csv` with `BIOMASS::fitDiamError()`), `"none"`, or a number giving the standard deviation of diameter measurement error in cm
* `quad_origin` -- Optional, alignment of the quadrat grid in each plot: `"centre"` (default) centres the grid in the plot, `"corner"` starts it at the origin corner of the plot, and `[x, y]` starts it x and y m from the origin corner. Where the plot dimensions are not a multiple of the quadrat dimensions, strips of the plot outside the grid are left out
* `missing_diam_method` -- Optional, how live stems without a diameter measurement are treated: `"impute"` (default) imputes their diameter in each Monte Carlo simulation from the other trees in the same plot, see [Missing measurements], or `"exclude"` excludes them
* `als_date` -- Optional, date of the airborne lidar acquisition matched to the plot data, `"YYYY-MM-DD"`, `"YYYY-MM"` or `"YYYY"`, used to report the time between the ALS acquisition and the census
* `taper_method` -- Optional, correction of diameters measured above 1.3 m to their equivalent at 1.3 m with an exponential taper model, used to estimate height and AGB: `"none"` (default), `"cushman2014"` (Cushman et al. 2014, Barro Colorado Island only) or `"cushman2021"` (Cushman et al. 2021, general model fitted at five lowland tropical forest sites). Palms are not corrected. Diameter thresholds use the measured diameter
* `taper_species` -- Optional, species terms of `"cushman2014"` by taxon name, e.g. `{"Ceiba pentandra": 0.0495}`
* `stem_allometry` -- Optional, `true` or `false` (default), whether stems use the AGB allometry in `agb_allometry` in the stem table, e.g. `"goodman2013"` for palms, see `agb_allometries` in `func.R`. Stems without one use Chave et al. (2014)
* `growth_form_exclude` -- Optional, values of `growth_form` in the stem table excluded from AGB density, e.g. `["strangler"]`. These stems have AGB estimates. None by default
* `height_custom` -- Required if `height_method` is `"custom"`, the height-diameter model: `formula`, height (m) as a function of diameter `D` (cm), e.g. `"a * D^b / (k + D^b)"`; `parameters`, e.g. `{a: 57.1, b: 0.73, k: 21.79}`; `sigma`, the residual standard deviation; `link`, `"log"` (default) if the residual error is log-normal and `formula` gives the median height, or `"identity"`; and `reference` 
* `crown_method` -- Optional, whether quadrat AGB density is also estimated with the AGB of each tree spread over its crown, see [Estimate quadrat AGBD and propagate error]: `"none"` (default) or `"custom"` (crown area from the allometry in `crown_custom`)
* `crown_custom` -- Required if `crown_method` is `"custom"`, the crown area allometry: `formula`, crown area (m^2^) as a function of diameter `D` (cm), e.g. `"a * D^b"`; `parameters`, e.g. `{a: 0.57, b: 1.34}`; `sigma`, the residual standard deviation; `link`, `"log"` (default) if the residual error is log-normal and `formula` gives the median crown area, or `"identity"`; and `reference`
* `rocrate` -- Information on who ran the workflow, used in the RO-Crate meta-data files which accompany each data product:
  * `author_name` -- e.g. `"John L. Godlee"`
  * `author_email` -- e.g. `"GodleeJ@si.edu"`
  * `author_orcid` -- Optional, ORCID URL of the author, e.g. `"https://orcid.org/0000-0000-0000-0000"`
  * `affiliation` -- e.g. `"Smithsonian Institution"`
  * `license` -- License file for the data products, e.g. `"TERMS.md"`

Import the example `param.yaml`:

```{r}
# Import param.yaml
# p <- yaml::read_yaml("./sites/<SITE>/<ACQUISITION>/<PRODUCTVERSION>/param.yaml")
p <- read_yaml(file.path(indir, "param.yaml"))

# Import software version
software_version <- read_yaml(file.path(indir, "version.yaml"))

# Merge parameters lists
param <- c(p, software_version)

# Define parameter names
param_name_vec <- c(
  "site_id",
  "acquisition_id",
  "quad_dim",
  "opt_s3",
  "s3_dir",
  "out_dir",
  "raw_dir",
  "raw_version",
  "height_method",
  "wd_method",
  "polygon_method",
  "outside_max_dist_m",
  "corner_outlier_dist_m",
  "quad_grid_tol",
  "height_model",
  "agbd_diam_min_cm",
  "include_broken",
  "multi_stem_method",
  "unmapped_method",
  "diam_error",
  "software_version",
  "product_version",
  "rocrate"
)

# Define optional parameter names
# `als_date` is the date of the airborne lidar acquisition matched to the
# plot data, YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM or YYYY, used in 12_report.R
# `quad_origin` is the alignment of the quadrat grid in each plot, see
# ./07_quad.R: "centre" (default), "corner", or an offset [x, y] in metres
# from the origin corner of each plot
# `missing_diam_method` is how live stems without a diameter measurement are
# treated, see ./08_agb_mc.R: "impute" (default) or "exclude"
# `taper_method` is the correction of diameters measured away from 1.3 m to
# their equivalent at 1.3 m, see `taperB()` in ./func.R: "none" (default),
# "cushman2014" (Barro Colorado Island only) or "cushman2021"
# `taper_species` is the species terms of "cushman2014", by taxon name, e.g.
# {"Ceiba pentandra": 0.0495}. Other species use the base class
# `stem_allometry` is whether stems use the AGB allometry in `agb_allometry`
# in the stem table, see `agb_allometries` in ./func.R: false (default) or
# true
# `growth_form_exclude` is values of `growth_form` in the stem table excluded
# from AGB density, e.g. ["strangler"]. None by default
# `height_custom` is the height-diameter model used if `height_method` is
# "custom", see `heightCustom()` in ./func.R
# `crown_method` is whether quadrat AGB density is also estimated with tree
# AGB spread over crowns, see ./08_agb_mc.R: "none" (default) or "custom"
# `crown_custom` is the crown area allometry used if `crown_method` is
# "custom", see `crownCustom()` in ./func.R
param_optional_vec <- c(
  "als_date",
  "quad_origin",
  "missing_diam_method",
  "taper_method",
  "taper_species",
  "stem_allometry",
  "growth_form_exclude",
  "height_custom",
  "crown_method",
  "crown_custom"
)

# Define RO-Crate parameter names, `author_orcid` is optional
rocrate_name_vec <- c(
  "author_name",
  "author_email",
  "affiliation",
  "license"
)

# Check all parameters present
# `s3_dir` is only needed if `opt_s3` is TRUE
param_missing <- setdiff(param_name_vec, names(param))
if (isFALSE(param$opt_s3)) {
  param_missing <- setdiff(param_missing, "s3_dir")
}
if (length(param_missing) > 0) {
  stop("Missing parameters: ", paste(param_missing, collapse = ", "))
}

rocrate_missing <- setdiff(rocrate_name_vec, names(param$rocrate))
if (length(rocrate_missing) > 0) {
  stop("Missing `rocrate` parameters: ", paste(rocrate_missing, collapse = ", "))
}

param_extra <- setdiff(names(param), c(param_name_vec, param_optional_vec))
if (length(param_extra) > 0) {
  warning("Unrecognised parameters: ", paste(param_extra, collapse = ", "))
}

# Check parameter values
param_choices <- list(
  height_method = c("regional", "field", "custom"),
  wd_method = c("regional", "field", "local"),
  polygon_method = c("exact", "affine", "procrustes"),
  height_model = c("best", "log1", "log2", "weibull", "michaelis"),
  multi_stem_method = c("equivalent", "stem"),
  unmapped_method = c("random", "exclude")
)
for (i in names(param_choices)) {
  if (!param[[i]] %in% param_choices[[i]]) {
    stop("`", i, "` must be one of: ", paste(param_choices[[i]], collapse = ", "))
  }
}

if (length(param$quad_dim) != 2 || !is.numeric(param$quad_dim)) {
  stop("`quad_dim` must be two numbers, e.g. [50, 50]")
}

if (length(param$raw_version) != 1 || !grepl("^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$", param$raw_version)) {
  stop("`raw_version` must be a single version string, e.g. \"v1\", ",
    "without underscores or dots")
}

if (length(param$outside_max_dist_m) != 1 || !is.numeric(param$outside_max_dist_m) ||
  param$outside_max_dist_m < 0) {
  stop("`outside_max_dist_m` must be a number >= 0")
}

if (length(param$corner_outlier_dist_m) != 1 || !is.numeric(param$corner_outlier_dist_m) ||
  param$corner_outlier_dist_m <= 0) {
  stop("`corner_outlier_dist_m` must be a number > 0")
}

if (length(param$quad_grid_tol) != 1 || !is.numeric(param$quad_grid_tol) ||
  param$quad_grid_tol < 0 || param$quad_grid_tol >= 1) {
  stop("`quad_grid_tol` must be a number >= 0 and < 1")
}

if (length(param$agbd_diam_min_cm) != 1 || !is.numeric(param$agbd_diam_min_cm) ||
  param$agbd_diam_min_cm < 0) {
  stop("`agbd_diam_min_cm` must be a number >= 0")
}

if (length(param$include_broken) != 1 || !is.logical(param$include_broken) ||
  is.na(param$include_broken)) {
  stop("`include_broken` must be true or false")
}

if (length(param$diam_error) != 1 ||
  !(param$diam_error %in% c("chave2004", "field", "none") ||
    (is.numeric(param$diam_error) && param$diam_error > 0))) {
  stop("`diam_error` must be \"chave2004\", \"field\", \"none\", or a ",
    "number > 0, the standard deviation of diameter measurement error in cm")
}

if (is.null(param$quad_origin)) {
  param$quad_origin <- "centre"
}
if (is.null(param$missing_diam_method)) {
  param$missing_diam_method <- "impute"
}
if (!identical(param$missing_diam_method, "impute") && 
  !identical(param$missing_diam_method, "exclude")) {
  stop("`missing_diam_method` must be one of: impute, exclude")
}

if (is.null(param$taper_method)) {
  param$taper_method <- "none"
}
if (!param$taper_method %in% c("none", "cushman2014", "cushman2021")) {
  stop("`taper_method` must be one of: none, cushman2014, cushman2021")
}
if (!is.null(param$taper_species) && (!is.list(param$taper_species) ||
  is.null(names(param$taper_species)) ||
  !all(vapply(param$taper_species, is.numeric, logical(1))))) {
  stop("`taper_species` must be taxon names with numeric species terms, ",
    "e.g. {\"Ceiba pentandra\": 0.0495}")
}

if (is.null(param$stem_allometry)) {
  param$stem_allometry <- FALSE
}
if (length(param$stem_allometry) != 1 || !is.logical(param$stem_allometry) ||
  is.na(param$stem_allometry)) {
  stop("`stem_allometry` must be true or false")
}

param$growth_form_exclude <- unlist(param$growth_form_exclude)
if (length(param$growth_form_exclude) > 0 && !is.character(param$growth_form_exclude)) {
  stop("`growth_form_exclude` must be values of `growth_form`, e.g. [\"strangler\"]")
}

if (param$height_method == "custom") {
  if (is.null(param$height_custom) ||
    !all(c("formula", "parameters", "sigma") %in% names(param$height_custom))) {
    stop("`height_method` is \"custom\", so `height_custom` must give the ",
      "height-diameter model's `formula`, `parameters` and `sigma`")
  }
  # Check the model can be built
  invisible(heightCustom(param$height_custom))
}

if (is.null(param$crown_method)) {
  param$crown_method <- "none"
}
if (!param$crown_method %in% c("none", "custom")) {
  stop("`crown_method` must be one of: none, custom")
}
if (param$crown_method == "custom") {
  if (is.null(param$crown_custom)) {
    stop("`crown_method` is \"custom\", so `crown_custom` must give the ",
      "crown area allometry's `formula`, `parameters` and `sigma`")
  }
  # Check the allometry can be built
  invisible(crownCustom(param$crown_custom))
}
if (!(identical(param$quad_origin, "centre") || identical(param$quad_origin, "corner") ||
  (is.numeric(param$quad_origin) && length(param$quad_origin) == 2 && 
    all(param$quad_origin >= 0)))) {
  stop("`quad_origin` must be \"centre\", \"corner\", or two numbers >= 0, ",
    "the offset of the quadrat grid from the origin corner of each plot in m, e.g. [10, 10]")
}

if (!is.null(param$als_date)) {
  param$als_date <- as.character(param$als_date)
  if (length(param$als_date) != 1 || is.na(decDate(param$als_date))) {
    stop("`als_date` must be a single date: YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM or YYYY")
  }
}

# Print parameters
param
```

If `opt_s3` is `true`, the `paws` package should be loaded to allow data data to be retrieved from an AWS S3 bucket. This is only relevant if data processing is happening on the [MAAP](https://docs.maap-project.org/en/hub/index.html) platform.

```{r}
# Optionally load AWS S3 package
if (param$opt_s3) {
  library(paws)
}
```

## Data structure 

GEO-TREES data products are organised in a strict directory hierarchy:

* SITE - The site name. Matches the `site_id` column in tree inventory datasets.
* DATATYPE - in this case "INV" tree inventory data. Alternatively, e.g. "ALS" (airborne laser scanning) or "TLS" (terrestrial laser scanning)
* ACQUISITION - The ID of the discrete period when L0 data was acquired in the field using a particular platform, normally including the date of acquisition in YYYY-MM-DD format. Where a L0 dataset was acquired over multiple days, prefer the mid-acquisition date. Tree inventory acquisitions are named by census year, i.e. the year of the mid-date of all stem measurements, in YYYY format.
* PRODUCT - Data product level, either:
  * "L0" - raw data 
  * "L1" - re-formatted raw data (raw instrument)
  * "L2" - model-derived products at matching resolution of L1 
  * "L3" - variables mapped to uniform space-time grid scales
* PRODUCTVERSION - Version of the code used to produce the data product, normally a GitHub release version of the code used to produce that data product.

Not all data products must utilise all levels of the directory hierarchy, and
certain products may include additional levels where specified, but the order
of the basic hierarchy does not change. This directory structure means that
sub-directory levels are never mixed within a parent directory. See below for a
breakdown of these levels:

Data product files are named according to the full directory hierarchy, with
levels separated by underscores (_), and a consistent suffix across files of a
given type within a product. Thus, hierarchy levels should not contain
underscores ("\_"). To prevent interference with file extensions, hierarchy
levels should also not contain dots (periods, "."). Both these characters
should be replaced with a hyphen ("-"). For example, for the tree inventory
(INV) L3 quadrat-level AGBD estimates for site "PanamaCanal", acquired on the
1st January 2025, processed using version 2.4 of the tree inventory processing
pipeline, using the v2 parameter set:

SITE: PanamaCanal
DATATYPE: INV
ACQUISITION: 2025-01-01
PRODUCTVERSION: v2
SOFTWAREVERSION: v2.4
PRODUCT: L3
File: quad

Directory path: PanamaCanal/INV/2025-01-01/v2/v2-4/L3/
Filename: PanamaCanal_INV_2025-01-01_v2_v2-4_L3_quad.gpkg

## Import L0 data

For convenience, we create a list `L0` where each element is a different L0
tree inventory data object. Column classes are taken from the column
templates in `./templates/`, so that e.g. an `acquisition_id` of `"2024"` is
read as a character string rather than a number.

```{r}
# Import column classes from column templates
colClass <- function(x) {
  cols <- read.csv(file.path("../../templates", paste0(x, "_cols.csv")))
  setNames(cols$class, cols$column_name)
}

# Import raw L0 data
L0 <- list(
  # Import stem measurements
  stem = read.csv(file.path(indir, "stem.csv"), colClasses = colClass("stem")),

  # Import plot meta-data
  plot = read.csv(file.path(indir, "plot.csv"), colClasses = colClass("plot")),

  # Import plot geo-location data
  pt = read.csv(file.path(indir, "pt.csv"), colClasses = colClass("pt")),

  # Import taxonomy data (optional)
  taxa = read.csv(file.path(indir, "taxa.csv"), colClasses = colClass("taxon")),

  # Import individual local wood density estimates (optional)
  wd = read.csv(file.path(indir, "wd.csv"), colClasses = colClass("wd")),

  # Import additional height-diameter measurements (optional)
  height = read.csv(file.path(indir, "hd.csv"), colClasses = colClass("height")),

  # Import field subplot bounds (optional)
  subplot = read.csv(file.path(indir, "subplot.csv"), colClasses = colClass("subplot"))
)
```

If you are on the MAAP platform and data is stored in an S3 bucket, use this
method to copy the files to a local directory first.

```{r}
# If S3, copy raw data from S3 bucket to local directory
if (param$opt_s3) {
  # Get object list from S3
  s3_client <- s3(region = "us-west-2")

  # Define S3 bucket where MAAP user directories are located
  # YOU MAY NEED CHANGE THIS
  bucket <- "maap-ops-workspace"

  # Identify files in dir_input
  s3_response <- s3_client$list_objects_v2(Bucket = bucket, Prefix = param$s3_dir)

  # Collect S3 paths from bucket
  shared_objects <- sapply(s3_response$Contents, "[[", "Key")

  # Check files detected
  if (length(shared_objects) == 0) { 
    stop("No raw data files detected in S3 bucket")
  }
  
  # Retrieve all files
  for (i in shared_objects) {
    # Construct new key in destination folder
    dest_key <- sub(param$s3_dir, param$raw_dir, i)

    # Copy files to local directory
    s3_client$download_file(Bucket = bucket, Key = i, Filename = dest_key)
  }
}
```

The stem measurement table contains one row per stem measurement. Stems may be
measured multiple times within a single census, for example if multiple
diameter measurements are collected at different Points of Measurement (POMs)
along the length of the stem.

The `record_id` column is a unique identifier for the stem measurement record
within the site, essentially the row number of the stem measurement table. 

The `measurement_date` column records the date of each measurement as a decimal
year, e.g. `2024.585` for 2nd August 2024, and `measurement_date_res` records
the resolution of the original date: `"YYYY-MM-DD"`, `"YYYY-MM"`, or `"YYYY"`.
The `decDate()` function converts dates to decimal years. Dates recorded only
to the month or year are placed at the middle of that month or year, e.g.
`decDate("2024")` returns `2024.5`.

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Example of L0 stem measurement table."
kable(head(L0$stem, 10))
```

The plot meta-data table contains one row per census per plot. It contains
additional information on field methodology, and qualitative information on
local environmental conditions and vegetation structure. These data are used
mostly for interpretation.

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Example of L0 plot meta-data table."
kable(L0$plot)
```

The plot geo-location table contains one row per location estimate of a single
survey point. Survey points may have multiple location estimates which are then
averaged when fitting the plot polygon. This table contains many columns
reserved for additional information provided when differential GNSS equipment
is used. In the example dataset these columns are blank ebcause the survey
points were collected with a single handheld GNSS unit. 

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Example of L0 plot geo-location measurements table."
kable(head(L0$pt, 5))
```

The optional taxa table contains additional taxonomic information. Each row is
a taxonomic name that features in the stem table, and columns contain corrected
taxonomic name information. This table is only used for interpretation. It is
useful in the case where codes or short-hand taxonomic names were used in the
field and those need to be linked with the full taxonomic name.

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Example of optional L0 taxa table."
kable(head(L0$taxa, 5))
```

The optional wood density table contains local field-measured wood density.
These measurements do not have to come from the plots, or even the same site,
but should be representative of the trees in the site. Each row is a taxonomic
name that features in the stem table. Where multiple wood density measurements
were collected for a single taxon, these should be aggregated to a mean,
standard deviation and the number of measurements.

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Example of optional L0 wood density estimates table."
kable(head(L0$wd, 5))
```

The optional stem height table contains local field-measured stem diameter and
height measurements. These measurements do not have to come from the plots, or
even the same site, but should be representative of the trees in the site. In
this case, the measurements were colelcted within the same site, but outside
the plots, hence the `site_id` column is filled, but the `plot_id` column is
filled with `NA` values.

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Example of optional L0 diameter-height measurements table."
kable(head(L0$height, 5))
```

Local biomass allometry

Local height-diameter allometry
:::

Before processing, `valCheck()` runs a series of checks on the L0 data objects.
It returns an error for values which would cause the processing to fail, or
which are impossible, e.g. negative stem diameters, plot IDs which don't match
between tables, or values outside the ranges given in the template files in
`./templates/`. It returns a warning for values which are probably wrong, but
which may be legitimate, e.g. stems mapped far outside the plot, stems
without a `stem_id`, or field subplots which overlap, or which extend outside
the plot.

```{r}
# Check values in L0 data
valCheck(
  plot = L0$plot,
  stem = L0$stem,
  pt = L0$pt,
  taxon = L0$taxa,
  height = L0$height,
  wd = L0$wd,
  subplot = L0$subplot)
```

The example data have a diameter and coordinates for every stem. To show how
missing measurements are handled, see [Missing measurements], we remove the
diameter of 10 live stems, the coordinates of one stem in each of 10
multi-stemmed trees, and the coordinates of all stems of 20 trees. This is
for illustration only, and is not part of the processing workflow.

```{r}
# Remove some measurements, to illustrate how missing measurements are handled
set.seed(1)
live <- which(grepl("A", L0$stem$code) & grepl("S", L0$stem$code) & 
  !grepl("T|M", L0$stem$code))
L0$stem$diam_cm[sample(live, 10)] <- NA

tree_key_eg <- paste(L0$stem$plot_id, L0$stem$tree_id)
multi <- intersect(live, which(tree_key_eg %in% tree_key_eg[duplicated(tree_key_eg)]))
multi_one <- multi[!duplicated(tree_key_eg[multi])]
xy_na <- c(
  sample(multi_one, min(10, length(multi_one))),
  which(tree_key_eg %in% sample(unique(tree_key_eg[live]), 20)))
L0$stem[xy_na, c("x_rel_m", "y_rel_m")] <- NA
```

## Correct taxonomy 

`02_taxa.R`

Here we combine all the taxonomic names recorded across all the L0 data
objects, then use the `BIOMASS::correctTaxo()` function to query the 
[World Flora Online](https://www.worldfloraonline.org/) (WFO) API to find
matching taxonomic names in their database. 

The argument `interactive = TRUE` means that when a name matches multiple
taxonomic names in the WFO database, users will be prompted to pick the correct
taxonomic name from a list in the R console. In the automated workflow,
prompts are only shown in an interactive R session. When processing many sites
with `zz_site_all.R`, which sets `options(inv.batch = TRUE)`, ambiguous names
are left unmatched so that processing isn't interrupted. These names can be
matched in a later interactive run.

Example of the interactive dialogue returned by `correctTaxo()` for the name `"Julbernardia pan"`:

```
--- Pick a name ---
Matching string:        julbernardia pan
1   wfo-4000019655      Julbernardia    Pellegr.        accepted        Code/Plantae/Pteridobiotina/Angiosperms/Fabales/Fabaceae/Detarioideae/Julbernardia
2   wfo-0000169035      Julbernardia baumii     (Harms) Troupin synonym Code/Plantae/Pteridobiotina/Angiosperms/Fabales/Fabaceae/Detarioideae/Julbernardia/paniculata$Julbernardia/baumii
3   wfo-0000169220      Julbernardia paniculata (Benth.) Troupin        accepted        Code/Plantae/Pteridobiotina/Angiosperms/Fabales/Fabaceae/Detarioideae/Julbernardia/paniculata
4   wfo-0000169080      Julbernardia normandii  Pellegr.        synonym Code/Plantae/Pteridobiotina/Angiosperms/Fabales/Fabaceae/Detarioideae/Julbernardia/brieyi$Julbernardia/normandii
5   wfo-0000169069      Julbernardia brieyi     (De Wild.) Troupin      accepted        Code/Plantae/Pteridobiotina/Angiosperms/Fabales/Fabaceae/Detarioideae/Julbernardia/brieyi
6   wfo-0000169273      Julbernardia seretii    (De Wild.) Troupin      accepted        Code/Plantae/Pteridobiotina/Angiosperms/Fabales/Fabaceae/Detarioideae/Julbernardia/seretii
7   wfo-0000169317      Julbernardia unijugata  J.Léonard       accepted        Code/Plantae/Pteridobiotina/Angiosperms/Fabales/Fabaceae/Detarioideae/Julbernardia/unijugata
8   wfo-0000169251      Julbernardia pellegriniana      Troupin accepted        Code/Plantae/Pteridobiotina/Angiosperms/Fabales/Fabaceae/Detarioideae/Julbernardia/pellegriniana
9   wfo-0000169284      Julbernardia ogoouensis Pellegr.        synonym Code/Plantae/Pteridobiotina/Angiosperms/Fabales/Fabaceae/Detarioideae/Julbernardia/seretii$Julbernardia/ogoouensis
10  wfo-0000169673      Julbernardia polyphylla (Harms) Troupin synonym Code/Plantae/Pteridobiotina/Angiosperms/Fabales/Fabaceae/Detarioideae/Tetraberlinia/polyphylla$Julbernardia/polyphylla

> Enter a number to pick a row from the list, a valid WFO ID, 'N' for the next page, 'P' for the previous page, 'S' or press Enter to skip:
```

In the example dataset the taxonomic names are strings containing the genus,
species, any infra-specific epithets such as variety (`var.`) or subspecies (`subsp.`), or a
higher-order taxonomic rank such as just the genus or family. Some examples of valid names:

* "Burkea africana"
* "Pseudolachnostylis maprouneifolia var. glabra"
* "Quercus"
* "Fagaceae"

`correctTaxo()` also allows the user to pass separate `genus` and `species`
(species epithet) columns if your data is formatted that way.

If `useCache = TRUE`, `correctTaxo()` creates a cache object containing
previously queried taxonomic names, including the choices made during
interactive matching. In the automated workflow this cache is saved with the
raw data, to `wfo_cache.rds` in the directory containing `raw_dir`, e.g.
`./dat/sites/<SITE>/INV/<ACQUISITION>/wfo_cache.rds`. It is shared by all
product versions of an acquisition, as a record of the choices made. Names are matched in chunks, and the cache is saved after
each chunk, so choices are kept if interactive matching is interrupted. Names
which could not be matched in a batch run are not saved, so they are offered
again in the next interactive run.

```{r}
# Combine taxa across tables
taxon_vec <- sort(unique(c(
  L0$stem$taxon_name,
  L0$wd$taxon_name,
  L0$height$taxon_name)))

# Load WFO cache from previous processing
loadWFOCache(file.path(indir, "wfo_cache.rds"))

# Prompt the user only in interactive sessions
taxa_interactive <- interactive() && !isTRUE(getOption("inv.batch"))

# Match names in chunks, saving the cache after each chunk
# In the vignette the cache is saved to a temporary file
wfo_path <- file.path(tempdir(), "wfo_cache.rds")
chunk_size <- 25
taxon_chunks <- split(taxon_vec, ceiling(seq_along(taxon_vec) / chunk_size))
taxa_list <- list()
for (i in seq_along(taxon_chunks)) {
  taxa_list[[i]] <- BIOMASS::correctTaxo(
    genus = taxon_chunks[[i]], 
    species = NULL,
    interactive = taxa_interactive, 
    preferAccepted = TRUE,
    preferFuzzy = FALSE,
    sub_pattern = subPattern(),
    useCache = TRUE,
    useAPI = TRUE,
    capacity = 60,
    fill_time_s = 1, 
    timeout = 60)

  saveWFOCache(wfo_path, rm_empty = !taxa_interactive)
}
stem_taxa_all <- bind_rows(taxa_list)

# Fill the family of names without a matched family, e.g. stems identified
# only to family, from the optional taxon table, so that wood density can be
# estimated at family level
if (!is.null(L0$taxa)) {
  taxon_family <- trimws(L0$taxa$taxon_family[match(stem_taxa_all$nameOriginal, L0$taxa$taxon_name)])
  family_fill <- is.na(stem_taxa_all$familyAccepted) & !is.na(taxon_family) & taxon_family != ""
  stem_taxa_all$familyAccepted[family_fill] <- taxon_family[family_fill]
}
```

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Example of output of `BIOMASS::correctTaxo()`."
# Inspect taxa table
kable(head(stem_taxa_all))
```

To make it easier to check the results, we create a table of names which were
changed (e.g. synonyms, spelling corrections) or which could not be matched,
with the method used to match each name and the number of stems affected. In
the automated workflow this table is written to `report/taxa_review.csv`. Methods
include `"AUTO"` (a single exact match), `"AUTO ACC"` (the only accepted name
among several candidates), `"MANUAL"` (picked by the user), `"SKIP"` (skipped
by the user), and `"EMPTY"` (no match found).

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Names changed or not matched during taxonomic name matching."
# Create table of names which were changed or not matched, for review
taxa_method <- vapply(stem_taxa_all$nameSubmitted, function(x) { 
  m <- BIOMASS::getWFOCache()[[x]]$method
  if (is.null(m) || is.na(x)) NA_character_ else m
}, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)

# Names are compared ignoring case and repeated whitespace
nameStd <- function(x) tolower(trimws(gsub("\\s+", " ", x)))

taxa_review <- stem_taxa_all %>%
  mutate(
    method = taxa_method,
    n_stem = as.vector(table(L0$stem$taxon_name)[nameOriginal]),
    n_stem = ifelse(is.na(n_stem), 0L, n_stem)) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(nameOriginal), nameOriginal != "",
    is.na(nameAccepted) | nameStd(nameOriginal) != nameStd(nameAccepted)) %>%
  dplyr::select(nameOriginal, nameAccepted, familyAccepted, method, n_stem) %>%
  arrange(is.na(nameAccepted), desc(n_stem))

kable(head(taxa_review, 10))
```

We also summarise the outcome of name matching by the number of stems
affected, to check whether names which could not be matched affect many
stems. In the automated workflow this table is written to
`02_taxa/taxa_outcome.csv`, and used in the site report.

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Outcome of taxonomic name matching, by number of names and stems."
# Summarise matching outcomes by number of stems
taxa_outcome <- stem_taxa_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(nameOriginal), nameOriginal != "") %>%
  mutate(
    n_stem = as.vector(table(L0$stem$taxon_name)[nameOriginal]),
    outcome = case_when(
      !is.na(nameAccepted) & nameStd(nameOriginal) == nameStd(nameAccepted) ~ "matched, unchanged",
      !is.na(nameAccepted) ~ "matched, changed",
      !is.na(familyAccepted) ~ "family only",
      TRUE ~ "not matched"),
    outcome = factor(outcome, levels = c("matched, unchanged",
      "matched, changed", "family only", "not matched"))) %>%
  group_by(outcome, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  summarise(n_name = n(), n_stem = sum(n_stem, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(pct_stem = round(100 * n_stem / sum(n_stem), 1))

kable(taxa_outcome)
```

## Estimate stem wood density

`03_wd.R`

Here we estimate the wood density of each stem measurement using the
`BIOMASS::getWoodDensity()` function, which uses taxonomic names to extract
wood density estimates at species, genus, or family level. These estimates
are provided by BIOMASS, from models fitted to version 2 of the Global Wood
Density Database [@Zanne2009]. Stems of taxa which are not in the database
are given the mean wood density of their plot.

```{r}
# Join taxonomy data to stem data
taxa_all <- left_join(L0$stem, stem_taxa_all, by = c("taxon_name" = "nameOriginal"))
```

In the example dataset there are local field-measured wood density estimates
that we can use. For `getWoodDensity()` to use them we need to summarise
individual measurements to the mean and standard deviation of each taxon. We
summarise by the accepted taxonomic name, so that different original names
which refer to the same taxon are pooled. Measurements without a wood density
value are excluded.

```{r}
# Optionally process local wood density data
wd_summ <- L0$wd %>%
  left_join(., stem_taxa_all, by = c("taxon_name" = "nameOriginal")) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(genusAccepted), !is.na(wood_density_gcm3)) %>% 
  mutate(wood_density_n = ifelse(is.na(wood_density_n), 1, wood_density_n)) %>% 
  group_by(
    family = familyAccepted, 
    genus = genusAccepted, 
    species = speciesAccepted) %>%
  summarise(
    wood_density_n_total = sum(wood_density_n),
    meanWD = sum(wood_density_gcm3 * wood_density_n) / wood_density_n_total,
    sdWD = {
      # If SD is NA, treat as 0 (no variance) 
      # but still account distance from grand mean
      clean_sd = ifelse(is.na(wood_density_sd_gcm3), 0, wood_density_sd_gcm3)
      
      # Components for grand variance
      ss_within  = sum((wood_density_n - 1) * clean_sd^2)
      ss_between = sum(wood_density_n * (wood_density_gcm3 - meanWD)^2)
      
      # If wood_density_n_total <= 1, return NA; otherwise calculate SD
      if (wood_density_n_total > 1) {
        sqrt((ss_within + ss_between) / (wood_density_n_total - 1)) 
      } else {
        NA_real_
      }
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(family, genus, species, meanWD, sdWD)
```

Then we estimate the wood density of each stem. Where a taxon has a local wood
density estimate with no standard deviation, e.g. from a single sample, and is
not in the Global Wood Density Database, we fill the missing standard
deviation with the mean standard deviation of other taxa estimated at the same
taxonomic level. Without a standard deviation, these stems would be dropped
from the AGB error propagation.

If `wd_method` is `"local"`, the Global Wood Density Database is not used.
Taxa without a local species estimate take the mean of the local species in
their genus, else in their family, where there are at least
`wd_local_min_sp` species, else the mean of all local species. Means are
taken over species, so that well-sampled species do not dominate, and the
standard deviation of a genus, family or dataset estimate is the standard
deviation among its species.

```{r}
# Estimate wood density for each stem measurement
# "regional" - Global Wood Density Database v2, with BIOMASS::getWoodDensity()
# "field" - local measurements, replacing GWDD v2 estimates of the same taxa,
#   with GWDD v2 for taxa without local measurements
# "local" - local measurements only
if (param$wd_method == "local") {
  wd_local_min_sp <- 2

  wd_sp <- wd_summ %>%
    filter(!is.na(species), species != "")
  # Mean and SD of species estimates in each genus or family
  wd_group <- function(level) {
    wd_sp %>%
      filter(!is.na(.data[[level]])) %>%
      group_by(group = .data[[level]]) %>%
      summarise(n_sp = n(), sdWD = sd(meanWD), meanWD = mean(meanWD),
        .groups = "drop") %>%
      filter(n_sp >= wd_local_min_sp)
  }
  wd_genus <- wd_group("genus")
  wd_family <- wd_group("family")

  i_sp <- match(paste(taxa_all$genusAccepted, taxa_all$speciesAccepted),
    paste(wd_sp$genus, wd_sp$species))
  i_gen <- match(taxa_all$genusAccepted, wd_genus$group)
  i_fam <- match(taxa_all$familyAccepted, wd_family$group)
  levelWD <- case_when(
    !is.na(i_sp) ~ "species",
    !is.na(i_gen) ~ "genus",
    !is.na(i_fam) ~ "family",
    TRUE ~ "dataset")
  wd_all <- data.frame(
    family = taxa_all$familyAccepted,
    genus = taxa_all$genusAccepted,
    species = taxa_all$speciesAccepted,
    stand = taxa_all$plot_id,
    meanWD = case_when(
      levelWD == "species" ~ wd_sp$meanWD[i_sp],
      levelWD == "genus" ~ wd_genus$meanWD[i_gen],
      levelWD == "family" ~ wd_family$meanWD[i_fam],
      TRUE ~ mean(wd_sp$meanWD)),
    sdWD = case_when(
      levelWD == "species" ~ wd_sp$sdWD[i_sp],
      levelWD == "genus" ~ wd_genus$sdWD[i_gen],
      levelWD == "family" ~ wd_family$sdWD[i_fam],
      TRUE ~ sd(wd_sp$meanWD)),
    levelWD = levelWD)
} else {
  wd_all <- BIOMASS::getWoodDensity(
    genus = taxa_all$genusAccepted,
    species = taxa_all$speciesAccepted,
    stand = taxa_all$plot_id,
    family = taxa_all$familyAccepted,
    addWoodDensityData = if (param$wd_method == "field") { wd_summ },
    verbose = TRUE)
}

# Check rows of output match stems
stopifnot(
  nrow(wd_all) == nrow(taxa_all),
  identical(as.character(wd_all$genus), as.character(taxa_all$genusAccepted)),
  identical(as.character(wd_all$species), as.character(taxa_all$speciesAccepted)))

# Fill missing wood density SD with the mean SD of other taxa estimated at the
# same level
sd_na <- is.na(wd_all$sdWD)
if (any(sd_na)) {
  sd_level <- wd_all %>% 
    filter(!is.na(sdWD)) %>% 
    distinct(genus, species, levelWD, sdWD) %>% 
    group_by(levelWD) %>% 
    summarise(sdWD_fill = mean(sdWD), .groups = "drop")
  sd_fill <- sd_level$sdWD_fill[match(wd_all$levelWD[sd_na], sd_level$levelWD)]
  sd_fill[is.na(sd_fill)] <- mean(sd_level$sdWD_fill)
  wd_all$sdWD[sd_na] <- sd_fill
}

# Create output dataframe
stem_wd_all <- cbind(record_id = taxa_all$record_id, wd_all)
```

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Example of output of `BIOMASS::getWoodDensity()`."
# Inspect output
kable(head(stem_wd_all))
```

We summarise the taxonomic level at which wood density was estimated for
each stem. Estimates from the plot mean are used where a stem has no matched
genus or family. Many stems estimated at the family level or from the plot
mean may indicate problems with taxonomic names.

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Wood density (g cm-3) by taxonomic level of the estimate."
# Summarise the taxonomic level of wood density estimates
wd_check <- stem_wd_all %>%
  mutate(level = ifelse(levelWD %in% c("species", "genus", "family", "dataset"),
    levelWD, "plot mean")) %>%
  mutate(level = factor(level, 
    levels = intersect(c("species", "genus", "family", "plot mean", "dataset"), level)))

wd_level <- wd_check %>%
  group_by(level) %>%
  summarise(
    n_stem = n(),
    meanWD_mean = mean(meanWD, na.rm = TRUE),
    meanWD_min = min(meanWD, na.rm = TRUE),
    meanWD_max = max(meanWD, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(pct_stem = round(100 * n_stem / sum(n_stem), 1), .after = n_stem)

kable(wd_level, digits = 3)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Wood density estimates at each taxonomic level of the estimate, for stems used to estimate AGB density. Y-axis scales differ between levels."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7
# Figure of wood density at each taxonomic level of the estimate, for stems
# used to estimate AGB density, see `agbdFilter()` in func.R
record_agbd <- agbdFilter(L0$stem, L0$plot, 
  recordFilter(L0$stem, L0$plot, missing_diam = param$missing_diam_method == "impute"),
  diam_min_cm = param$agbd_diam_min_cm,
  include_broken = param$include_broken,
  growth_form_exclude = param$growth_form_exclude)
wd_fig <- filter(wd_check, as.character(record_id) %in% record_agbd)
wdLevelPlot(wd_fig$meanWD, wd_fig$level) +
  labs(
    title = "Wood density estimates by taxonomic level")
```

## Estimate stem height

`04_height.R`

Here we estimate the height of each stem measurement. Height estimates are
required for most stem AGB allometries.

There are multiple approaches to estimating stem height. In general, we
recommend this approach:

If there is an appropriate existing local height-diameter allometry, use that
to estimate the height of all stems in the site. A local height-diameter
allometry is deemed appropriate if the underlying data approximately span the
range of stem heights measured in the tree inventory data, the species
composition is similar to that found in the tree inventory data, and the local
conditions (water availability, temperature, topography) of the location where
the underlying data were collected are similar to that of the GEO-TREES site.

Otherwise if there is no existing local height-diameter allometry available, if
you have at least 50 local and reliable estimates of stem height and diameter,
spanning the range of stem size across the plots, fit a local height-diameter
allometry using the `BIOMASS::modelHD()` function.

Finally, if neither of the above are appropriate, use the
`BIOMASS::retrieveH()` function and supply plot coordinates to estimate stem
height from a regional height-diameter allometry [@Chave2014].

Height-diameter and AGB allometries use the diameter at 1.3 m. Where the
diameter of buttressed or irregular stems was measured higher up, the diameter
at 1.3 m can optionally be estimated with an exponential taper model, $d = D
e^{-b(h - 1.3)}$, where $d$ is the diameter measured at height $h$ and $D$ is
the diameter at 1.3 m, set by `taper_method`. `"cushman2014"` uses the model
of @Cushman2014 for Barro Colorado Island, Panama, with optional species terms
in `taper_species`. `"cushman2021"` uses the general model of @Cushman2021,
fitted at five lowland tropical forest sites, without its site effect. Only
stems measured above 1.3 m are corrected, as the taper models were fitted to
stems measured above buttresses, and palms are not corrected. The corrected
diameter is used to estimate height and AGB, while the measured diameter,
`diam_cm_meas`, is used for diameter thresholds, as the plots were sampled on
measured diameters. The example data use the default, `"none"`.

```{r}
# Diameter at 1.3 m, corrected for taper, see `taper_method` in param.yaml
# and `taperB()` in func.R. Stems without a POM were measured at the default
# POM of the plot
stem_taper <- L0$stem
stem_taper$diam_cm_meas <- stem_taper$diam_cm
if (param$taper_method != "none") {
  hom <- coalesce(stem_taper$pom_m,
    L0$plot$meas_pom_default_m[match(stem_taper$plot_id, L0$plot$plot_id)])
  wd_i <- match(stem_taper$record_id, stem_wd_all$record_id)
  palm <- stem_wd_all$family[wd_i] %in% "Arecaceae"
  sp_term <- unlist(param$taper_species)[
    paste(stem_wd_all$genus[wd_i], stem_wd_all$species[wd_i])]
  sp_term[is.na(sp_term)] <- 0
  b <- taperB(stem_taper$diam_cm, hom, param$taper_method,
    wd = stem_wd_all$meanWD[wd_i], sp_term = sp_term)
  taper_corr <- !palm & !is.na(stem_taper$diam_cm) & !is.na(hom) & hom > 1.3 + 1e-6
  stem_taper$diam_cm[taper_corr] <- stem_taper$diam_cm[taper_corr] /
    exp(-b[taper_corr] * (hom[taper_corr] - 1.3))
}
```

Where an existing local height-diameter allometry is available
(`height_method: "custom"`), it is given in `height_custom`, and built with
`BIOMASS::customHD()`, through `heightCustom()` in `func.R`. Its residual
error, `sigma`, is propagated to AGB in [Estimate quadrat AGBD and propagate
error]. With `link: "log"`, the residual error is log-normal, `formula` gives
the median height, and `retrieveH()` returns the mean height. The example data
have no local allometry, so here we use the model of @MartinezCano2019 for
Barro Colorado Island to illustrate:

```{r}
# Published height-diameter model, see `height_custom` in param.yaml
height_custom <- if (!is.null(param$height_custom)) {
  param$height_custom
} else {
  list(
    formula = "a * D^b / (k + D^b)",
    parameters = list(a = 57.1, b = 0.73, k = 21.79),
    sigma = 0.181,
    link = "log",
    reference = "Martinez-Cano et al. (2019)")
}
height_mod_custom <- heightCustom(height_custom)
height_mod_custom

# Predict mean height. For a model with log-normal error, the RSE is on the
# log scale
height_est_custom <- retrieveH(
  D = stem_taper$diam_cm,
  model = height_mod_custom)

# Create output dataframe, if `height_method` is "custom"
if (param$height_method == "custom") {
  stem_height_all <- stem_taper %>%
    mutate(
      height_m_pred = height_est_custom$H,
      height_m_pred_rse = height_est_custom$RSE) %>%
    dplyr::select(record_id, height_m_pred, height_m_pred_rse)
}
```


Where sufficient local height data are available:

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Fitted height-diameter models of different forms."
# Compare height diameter models
height_mod_comp <- modelHD(
  D = L0$height$diam_cm,
  H = L0$height$height_m,
  bayesian = FALSE,
  useCache = FALSE,
  drawGraph = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Example of output of `BIOMASS::modelHD() model fit comparison table`."
# Inspect tabular output of modelHD()
kable(height_mod_comp)
```

```{r}
# Choose height diameter model, set by `height_model`. If "best", use the
# model with the lowest residual standard error, calculated on the
# untransformed height scale for all models, so comparable across log and
# non-log models
height_mod_best <- if (param$height_model == "best") {
  height_mod_comp$method[which.min(height_mod_comp$RSE)]
} else {
  param$height_model
}

# Fit best height diameter model
height_mod <- modelHD(
  D = L0$height$diam_cm,
  H = L0$height$height_m,
  method = height_mod_best,
  bayesian = FALSE,
  useCache = FALSE,
  drawGraph = FALSE)

# Predict with best height diameter model
height_est <- retrieveH(
  D = stem_taper$diam_cm,
  model = height_mod)

# Create output dataframe, if `height_method` is "field"
if (param$height_method == "field") {
  stem_height_all <- stem_taper %>% 
    mutate(
      height_m_pred = height_est$H,
      height_m_pred_rse = height_est$RSE) %>% 
    dplyr::select(record_id, height_m_pred, height_m_pred_rse)
}
```

We choose the model with the lowest residual standard error (RSE). Note that
`Average_bias` is signed, so choosing the model with the lowest
`Average_bias` would choose the model which most underestimates stem height.

Alternatively using a regional height-diameter allometry where no height data
are available. `retrieveH()` estimates height from Equation 6a of
@Chave2014, using an index of environmental stress (E) at the centre of each
plot. The residual standard error of this model (0.243) is on the log scale,
so it is not a standard deviation of height in metres.

```{r}
# Extract plot centres
plot_pt_split <- L0$pt %>% 
  filter(!is.na(rover_easting_utm_m), !is.na(rover_northing_utm_m)) %>% 
  split(., .$crs_epsg)
p_cent <- bind_rows(lapply(plot_pt_split, function(x) { 
  st_as_sf(x, coords = c("rover_easting_utm_m", "rover_northing_utm_m"), 
    crs = unique(x$crs_epsg)) %>% 
  st_transform(., 4326) 
})) %>% 
group_by(site_id, plot_id) %>% 
summarise() %>% 
st_centroid() %>% 
cbind(., st_coordinates(.)) %>% 
st_drop_geometry() %>% 
dplyr::select(plot_id, X, Y)

# Add plot centres to stem data
s_cent <- stem_taper %>% 
  left_join(., p_cent, by = "plot_id")

stopifnot(all(!is.na(s_cent$X)))
stopifnot(all(!is.na(s_cent$Y)))

# Retrieve stem heights using plot locations
height_pred <- retrieveH(
  D = s_cent$diam_cm, 
  coord = s_cent[,c("X", "Y")])

# RSE of Chave et al. (2014) Eq. 6a, on the log scale
# NOTE: not a standard deviation in metres, do not pass to AGBmonteCarlo(errH = )
height_pred$RSE <- rep(0.243, length(height_pred$H))

s_cent$height_m_pred <- height_pred$H
s_cent$height_m_pred_rse <- height_pred$RSE

# Create output dataframe, if `height_method` is "regional"
if (param$height_method == "regional") {
  stem_height_all <- s_cent %>% 
    dplyr::select(record_id, height_m_pred, height_m_pred_rse)
}
```

We summarise the predicted stem heights. Heights over 60 m are rare, and may
indicate errors in stem diameter.

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Summary of predicted stem height."
# Height-diameter model used to estimate AGB, if `height_method` is "custom"
if (param$height_method == "custom") {
  height_mod <- height_mod_custom
}

# Summarise predicted heights
height_check <- stem_taper %>%
  dplyr::select(record_id, plot_id, diam_cm) %>%
  inner_join(., stem_height_all, by = "record_id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(diam_cm), !is.na(height_m_pred))

height_summ <- height_check %>%
  summarise(
    n_stem = n(),
    height_m_min = min(height_m_pred),
    height_m_median = median(height_m_pred),
    height_m_max = max(height_m_pred),
    n_over_60m = sum(height_m_pred > 60))

kable(height_summ, digits = 2)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Stem height against diameter: measured heights, and predicted heights for stems used to estimate AGB density, drawn on top."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
# Figure of stem height against diameter, for stems used to estimate AGB
# density, see `agbdFilter()` in func.R. Measured heights are from the
# height table, or from the stem table if there is no height table. 
# Predicted heights are drawn on top of measured heights
height_pred_fig <- filter(height_check, as.character(record_id) %in% record_agbd)
height_obs <- if (!is.null(L0$height)) {
  filter(L0$height, !is.na(diam_cm), !is.na(height_m))
} else {
  filter(L0$stem, !is.na(diam_cm), !is.na(height_m))
}
p_height <- ggplot()
if (nrow(height_obs) > 0) {
  p_height <- p_height +
    geom_point(data = height_obs, aes(x = diam_cm, y = height_m, colour = "Measured"),
      size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5, shape = 16)
}
p_height <- p_height +
  geom_point(data = height_pred_fig, aes(x = diam_cm, y = height_m_pred, 
    colour = "Predicted"), size = 0.6, alpha = 0.3, shape = 16)
if (param$height_method == "field") {
  height_curve <- data.frame(diam_cm = seq(min(height_obs$diam_cm), 
    max(height_obs$diam_cm), length.out = 200))
  height_curve$height_m <- retrieveH(D = height_curve$diam_cm, model = height_mod)$H
  p_height <- p_height +
    geom_line(data = height_curve, aes(x = diam_cm, y = height_m, 
      colour = "Fitted model"), linewidth = 0.7)
}
p_height +
  scale_colour_manual(NULL, 
    values = c("Measured" = fig_pal$series[2], "Predicted" = fig_pal$series[1], 
      "Fitted model" = fig_pal$ink),
    breaks = c("Measured", "Predicted", "Fitted model")) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1, size = 2))) +
  labs(
    title = "Stem height against diameter",
    x = "Diameter (cm)", 
    y = "Height (m)") +
  themeFig()
```

## Estimate stem AGB 

`05_agb_stem.R`

Here we estimate the above-ground woody biomass (AGB, `agb_Mg`) of each stem
measurement using the `BIOMASS::computeAGB()` function, which returns the AGB
of each tree in Mg. Where heights come from a local
height-diameter model, fitted to the height data (`height_method: "field"`) or
published (`height_method: "custom"`), Equation 4 from @Chave2014
is used to estimate AGB with stem diameter (`D`), stem height (`H`), and wood
density (`WD`). Where no local height data are available (`height_method:
"regional"`), Equation 7 from @Chave2014 is used, which replaces stem height
with an index of environmental stress at the plot centre. This matches the
allometry used in the AGB error propagation in [Estimate quadrat AGBD and
propagate error], so that stem-level and quadrat-level estimates are
consistent. Because the @Chave2014 model
was fitted using mostly data from tropical wet forests, it may fail to
accurately capture the relationship between stem diameter, height, and volume
in other vegetation types. For these sites, a local AGB allometry may be more
appropriate. 

You may also choose to have different AGB allometries for different functional
groups in the tree inventory data. For example, if there are large baobab trees
(_Adansonia_ sp.), bamboos, palms, or lianas which have drastically different
physiognomy to other trees in the dataset. If `stem_allometry` is `true`, each
tree uses the allometry in `agb_allometry` of its largest stem in the stem
table, one of `agb_allometries` in `func.R`, e.g. `"goodman2013"`, the palm
allometry of @Goodman2013. Trees without one use @Chave2014. Each allometry in
`agb_allometries` is given in the format of the `fitted_allom` argument of
`BIOMASS::AGBmonteCarlo()`, as a formula of `D`, `H` and `WD`, its parameters
and residual standard deviation, and a link, so that its residual error is
propagated in [Estimate quadrat AGBD and propagate error]. Here, with a log
link, `agbAllomMean()` gives the mean of the log-normal distribution of AGB.
The example data do not use stem allometries.

Diameters are corrected for taper if `taper_method` is set, see [Estimate
stem height]. Basal area is calculated from the measured diameter.

Where trees have multiple stems, AGB is estimated for the tree from its
equivalent diameter, $D_{eq} = \sqrt{\sum D_i^2}$, the diameter of a single
stem with the same basal area as all its stems. Estimating AGB for each stem
separately would underestimate the AGB of multi-stemmed trees, because AGB
increases more than proportionally with stem diameter. Tree AGB is then shared
among its stems in proportion to their basal area. Trees are formed from the
stems used to estimate AGB density (see [Filter stem data]), grouped by
`tree_id` within each plot, using `recordFilter()`, `agbdFilter()` and
`treeEquiv()` from `func.R`. Other stems, e.g. dead stems, and stems below the
minimum diameter threshold of the plot, are treated as single-stemmed trees.
Wood density depends on taxonomic identity, which is the same for all stems of
a tree, so the wood density of the largest stem is used.

We also create some additional variables like stem basal area (`ba_m2`) and
stem volume (`volume_m3`).

```{r}
# Stems which form multi-stemmed trees. If `multi_stem_method` is "stem", AGB
# is estimated for each stem separately
record_agbd <- agbdFilter(stem_taper, L0$plot, 
  recordFilter(stem_taper, L0$plot, missing_diam = param$missing_diam_method == "impute"),
  diam_min_cm = param$agbd_diam_min_cm,
  include_broken = param$include_broken,
  growth_form_exclude = param$growth_form_exclude)
tree_include <- if (param$multi_stem_method == "equivalent") record_agbd else character(0)

# Join wood density, height, and equivalent diameter to stem data. Diameters
# are corrected for taper, see `taper_method`
stem_all <- stem_taper %>%
  left_join(., stem_wd_all, by = "record_id") %>%
  left_join(., stem_height_all, by = "record_id") %>%
  left_join(., treeEquiv(stem_taper, tree_include), by = "record_id")

# One row per tree. Wood density depends on taxonomic identity, which is the
# same for all stems of a tree, so the wood density of the largest stem is used
tree <- stem_all %>%
  arrange(desc(ba_share)) %>%
  group_by(tree_key) %>%
  summarise(
    plot_id = first(plot_id),
    diam_eq_cm = first(diam_eq_cm),
    meanWD = first(meanWD),
    agb_allometry = if (param$stem_allometry) first(agb_allometry) else NA_character_,
    n_taxa = n_distinct(taxon_name),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(agb_allometry = coalesce(na_if(agb_allometry, ""), "chave2014"))

allom_unknown <- setdiff(tree$agb_allometry, c("chave2014", names(agb_allometries)))
if (length(allom_unknown) > 0) {
  stop("Unknown `agb_allometry` in the stem table: ", 
    paste(allom_unknown, collapse = ", "), ". Must be one of: ",
    paste(c("chave2014", names(agb_allometries)), collapse = ", "))
}

if (any(tree$n_taxa > 1)) {
  warning(sum(tree$n_taxa > 1), " multi-stemmed trees have stems with ",
    "different taxonomic names. The wood density of the largest stem is used",
    call. = FALSE)
}

# Estimate tree-level AGB
# computeAGB() returns a vector of tree AGB in Mg. Stems without a diameter,
# see `missing_diam_method` in param.yaml, have no AGB estimate here. Their 
# diameters are imputed during AGB error propagation
muffleNA <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("NA values in D", conditionMessage(w))) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
}
if (param$height_method == "regional") {
  tree <- left_join(tree, p_cent, by = "plot_id")
  stopifnot(all(!is.na(tree$X)))
  tree$agb_Mg <- withCallingHandlers(BIOMASS::computeAGB(
    D = tree$diam_eq_cm,
    WD = tree$meanWD,
    coord = as.matrix(tree[, c("X", "Y")])), warning = muffleNA)
} else if (param$height_method %in% c("field", "custom")) {
  tree$agb_Mg <- withCallingHandlers(BIOMASS::computeAGB(
    D = tree$diam_eq_cm,
    WD = tree$meanWD,
    H = retrieveH(D = tree$diam_eq_cm, model = height_mod)$H), warning = muffleNA)
}

# Trees with other allometries, see `stem_allometry`
for (a in intersect(names(agb_allometries), tree$agb_allometry)) {
  i <- which(tree$agb_allometry == a)
  tree$agb_Mg[i] <- agbAllomMean(agb_allometries[[a]],
    D = tree$diam_eq_cm[i],
    H = if (param$height_method != "regional") retrieveH(D = tree$diam_eq_cm[i], model = height_mod)$H,
    WD = tree$meanWD[i])
}

# Share tree AGB among stems
stem_agb_all <- stem_all %>%
  mutate(
    agb_Mg = tree$agb_Mg[match(tree_key, tree$tree_key)] * ba_share,
    # Basal area from the measured diameter
    ba_m2 = base::pi * (diam_cm_meas / 2)^2 / 10000,
    volume_m3 = agb_Mg / meanWD) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    record_id,
    agb_Mg,
    ba_m2,
    volume_m3)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Histogram of stem-level Above-ground woody biomass (AGB) estimates."
# Visualise distribution of stem-level AGB
ggplot(stem_agb_all, aes(x = agb_Mg)) + 
  geom_histogram(colour = "black", fill = "grey", binwidth = 1, boundary = 0) + 
  theme_bw() + 
  labs(
    x = "Above-ground woody biomass (Mg)",
    y = "N stems")
```

We summarise the AGB of stems used to estimate AGB density in each plot,
using the nominal plot area, and list the trees with the largest AGB, which
may indicate data errors, e.g. diameters in mm rather than cm. Quadrat-level
AGB density, from the fitted plot polygons, is estimated in [Estimate
quadrat AGBD and propagate error].

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "AGB density in each plot, using nominal plot area."
# Summarise AGB of stems used to estimate AGB density in each plot
agb_plot <- L0$stem %>%
  dplyr::select(record_id, plot_id) %>%
  inner_join(., stem_agb_all, by = "record_id") %>%
  filter(as.character(record_id) %in% record_agbd) %>%
  group_by(plot_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_stem = n(),
    agb_Mg = sum(agb_Mg, na.rm = TRUE),
    ba_m2 = sum(ba_m2, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Plots with no stems used to estimate AGB density have zero AGB
  right_join(., dplyr::select(L0$plot, plot_id, plot_length_m, plot_width_m), 
    by = "plot_id") %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(n_stem, agb_Mg, ba_m2), ~ifelse(is.na(.x), 0, .x)),
    area_ha = plot_length_m * plot_width_m / 10000,
    agbd_Mg_ha = agb_Mg / area_ha,
    ba_m2_ha = ba_m2 / area_ha) %>%
  dplyr::select(plot_id, n_stem, area_ha, agb_Mg, agbd_Mg_ha, ba_m2_ha) %>%
  arrange(desc(agbd_Mg_ha))

kable(agb_plot, digits = 2)
```

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Trees with the largest AGB."
# Largest trees, which may indicate data errors, e.g. diameter in mm not cm
tree_large <- tree %>%
  filter(!is.na(agb_Mg)) %>%
  arrange(desc(agb_Mg)) %>%
  head(10) %>%
  dplyr::select(tree_key, plot_id, diam_eq_cm, meanWD, agb_Mg)

kable(tree_large, digits = 3)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Tree AGB against diameter, on log scales, using the equivalent diameter of multi-stemmed trees. Points far from the main cloud may be data errors."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
# Figure of tree AGB against equivalent diameter
tree_check <- filter(tree, !is.na(agb_Mg), agb_Mg > 0, diam_eq_cm > 0)
p_agb <- ggplot(tree_check, aes(x = diam_eq_cm, y = agb_Mg)) +
  geom_point(colour = fig_pal$series[1], size = 0.6, alpha = 0.3, shape = 16) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "Tree AGB against diameter",
    x = "Diameter (cm)",
    y = "AGB (Mg)") +
  themeFig()
p_agb
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Share of AGB in each 10 cm diameter class, for trees used to estimate AGB density, using the equivalent diameter of multi-stemmed trees. Numbers above the bars are the number of trees in each class."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
# Figure of the share of AGB in each diameter class, for trees used to
# estimate AGB density, all plots. Classes from `diam_class_max_cm` upwards
# are combined
diam_class_cm <- 10
diam_class_max_cm <- 150
tree_agbd <- tree %>%
  filter(tree_key %in% stem_all$tree_key[as.character(stem_all$record_id) %in% record_agbd],
    !is.na(agb_Mg))
diam_class <- tree_agbd %>%
  mutate(diam_class = pmin(floor(diam_eq_cm / diam_class_cm) * diam_class_cm, 
    diam_class_max_cm)) %>%
  group_by(diam_class) %>%
  summarise(n_tree = n(), agb_Mg = sum(agb_Mg), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    pct_agb = 100 * agb_Mg / sum(agb_Mg),
    label = ifelse(diam_class == diam_class_max_cm, paste0(diam_class_max_cm, "+"),
      paste0(diam_class, "-", diam_class + diam_class_cm)),
    label = factor(label, levels = label))
p_diam_class <- ggplot(diam_class, aes(x = label, y = pct_agb)) +
  geom_col(fill = fig_pal$series[1], width = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = format(n_tree, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)),
    vjust = -0.4, size = 3, colour = fig_pal$ink_muted) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(
    title = "Share of AGB by diameter class",
    x = "Diameter class (cm)",
    y = "Share of AGB (%)") +
  themeFig() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
p_diam_class
```
