## Filter stem data 

`06_record_fil.R`

Here we filter the tree inventory data prior to estimating above-ground biomass
density in each 50x50 m quadrat. 

We apply the following filters:

* Remove stems with no diameter measurement, if `missing_diam_method` is `"exclude"`. 
* Include only living stems.
* Include only standing stems.
* Remove stems that are broken below the diameter Point of Measurement (POM). Stems broken above the POM are included.
* Remove "missing" stems. I.e. stems which were not measured during the census.
* Where stems were measured multiple times at multiple POMs, choose the measurement with a diameter, then the highest POM, latest measurement date, and largest diameter measurement. Stems without a `stem_id` cannot be matched across measurements, so each of their records is treated as a separate stem.

Stems with a diameter below the minimum diameter threshold of the plot have
their own AGB estimates, but are not part of multi-stemmed trees, and are
excluded when AGB is summed to estimate AGB density, so that AGB density
matches the sampling of the plot. Stems without a diameter are assumed to be
at or above the threshold, as they were recorded in the census. The threshold
applies to the measured diameter, not the diameter corrected for taper. Stems
of growth forms listed in `growth_form_exclude`, from `growth_form` in the
stem table, e.g. strangler figs, whose stems are fused around a host tree,
are also excluded from AGB density.

```{r}
# Select stems used to estimate AGB, see `recordFilter()` in func.R
# Stems without coordinates are kept, and are placed at random during AGB 
# error propagation. If `missing_diam_method` is "impute", stems without a 
# diameter are kept, and their diameters are imputed during AGB error 
# propagation
record_fil <- recordFilter(L0$stem, L0$plot, 
  missing_diam = param$missing_diam_method == "impute")

# Select stems used to estimate AGB density, see `agbdFilter()` in func.R
# Stems below the minimum diameter threshold, the larger of
# `agbd_diam_min_cm` and the threshold of the plot, are excluded. Stems broken
# above the POM are excluded if `include_broken` is false, and stems of growth
# forms in `growth_form_exclude` are excluded
record_agbd <- agbdFilter(L0$stem, L0$plot, record_fil,
  diam_min_cm = param$agbd_diam_min_cm,
  include_broken = param$include_broken,
  growth_form_exclude = param$growth_form_exclude)
```

We summarise why stem records are excluded from AGB estimates and AGB
density. Each record is counted once, under the first reason which applies,
in the order of the checks in `recordFilter()` and `agbdFilter()`. "AGB
only" stems have AGB estimates, but are not included in AGB density.

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Stem records used to estimate AGB and AGB density, and reasons for excluding records."
# Summarise why stem records are excluded from AGB estimates and AGB density
diam_min <- pmax(L0$plot$meas_diam_min_cm[match(L0$stem$plot_id, L0$plot$plot_id)],
  param$agbd_diam_min_cm)
record_status <- L0$stem %>%
  mutate(
    status = case_when(
      as.character(record_id) %in% record_agbd & is.na(diam_cm) ~ 
        "included in AGB density, diameter imputed",
      as.character(record_id) %in% record_agbd ~ "included in AGB density",
      is.na(code) | code == "" ~ "excluded: no code",
      grepl("M", code) ~ "excluded: missing",
      !grepl("A", code) ~ "excluded: dead",
      !grepl("S", code) ~ "excluded: not standing",
      grepl("T", code) ~ "excluded: broken below POM",
      is.na(diam_cm) ~ "excluded: no diameter",
      !as.character(record_id) %in% record_fil ~ "excluded: repeat measurement of stem",
      !is.na(diam_min) & !is.na(diam_cm) & diam_cm < diam_min ~ 
        "AGB only: below diameter threshold",
      grepl("B", code) & !param$include_broken ~ "AGB only: broken above POM",
      growth_form %in% param$growth_form_exclude ~
        paste0("AGB only: excluded growth form (", growth_form, ")"),
      TRUE ~ "AGB only: other")) %>%
  count(status, name = "n_record") %>%
  mutate(pct_record = round(100 * n_record / sum(n_record), 1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(grepl("^included", status)), desc(n_record))

kable(record_status)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Diameter of stems used to estimate AGB density, all plots, in 5 cm classes."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
# Figure of the diameter of stems used to estimate AGB density, all plots.
# Stems without a diameter are not shown
diam_hist_cm <- 5
ggplot(filter(L0$stem, as.character(record_id) %in% record_agbd, !is.na(diam_cm)), 
  aes(x = diam_cm)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = diam_hist_cm, boundary = min(diam_min, na.rm = TRUE),
    fill = fig_pal$series[1], colour = fig_pal$surface, linewidth = 0.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Stem diameter",
    x = "Diameter (cm)", 
    y = "Stems") +
  themeFig()
```

### Missing measurements

Ideally every live stem would have a diameter and coordinates. Rather than
excluding stems with missing measurements, which would underestimate AGBD,
the uncertainty in their size or location is propagated to quadrat AGBD:

* Stems without a diameter, if `missing_diam_method` is `"impute"`, have
  their diameter imputed in each Monte Carlo simulation by
  `BIOMASS::AGBmonteCarlo()`, from the simulated diameter of a tree drawn at
  random from the other trees in the same plot. Their height and AGB are estimated
  from the imputed diameter. They have no AGB estimate in [Estimate stem
  AGB].
* Stems without coordinates in trees where other stems have coordinates are
  given the mean coordinates of the other stems of the tree, see [Fit plot
  spatial polygons].
* Trees where no stems have coordinates, if `unmapped_method` is `"random"`,
  are placed at a random location within their field subplot, if its
  position is known, otherwise within their plot, in each simulation, by
  `BIOMASS::subplot_summary()`, see [Estimate quadrat AGBD and propagate
  error].

## Fit plot spatial polygons

`07_quad.R`

Here, we create spatial polygons representing the area of each plot, using
field-measured geo-location estimates of survey points collected with GNSS
devices. See the [GEO-TREES Plot Geo-location Protocol](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OhKswemZykDQaX7irfUTQI0AuXsUJuYtQf_9SPV3WI0/edit?usp=sharing) for more guidance on
how to collect these data. We use the `BIOMASS::plotPolygonFit()` function to
do this.

`plotPolygonFit()` also projects stem map coordinates into a global coordinate
reference system.

In this example we use the `method = "procrustes"` algorithm to fit the plot
polygon, as specified by `polygon_method` in `param.yaml`, but you could also
use the "affine" or "exact" methods depending on the availability and quality
of the GNSS data, and the shape of the plot.

The "procrustes" method applies a rigid spatial transformation to align local
field coordinates with geographic projected coordinates. The algorithm
calculates the optimal two-dimensional translation (shifting) and rotation
needed to best fit the local plot corners to the provided GPS measurements.
Unlike the "affine" or "exact" algorithms, this method strictly preserves the
internal geometry, shape, and dimensions of the original field plot, i.e. we
trust the nominal dimensions of the field plot. By applying the resulting
rotation matrix and translation vector uniformly to both the plot corners and
the internal tree coordinates, the function ensures that all field-measured
distances and spatial relationships between trees are perfectly maintained in
the final geographic projection. This method is especially robust for
identifying outlier GPS measurements that deviate from the rigid, known shape
of the plot.

The "affine" method uses Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) linear regression to map
local field coordinates to geographic coordinates. By fitting separate linear
models for the X and Y axes, this method finds the optimal affine
transformation, allowing for translation, rotation, independent axis scaling,
and shearing that minimizes the overall squared error between the local corners
and the GPS measurements. The resulting linear models are then used to predict
the geographic locations of internal trees. While this method preserves
parallel lines and uniform point distributions, it may alter the overall scale
and internal angles of the original plot geometry.

The "exact" method requires exactly four plot corners. It determines the final
geographic location of each corner by calculating the simple average of its
corresponding GNSS measurements. To project the internal tree coordinates, the
algorithm utilizes bilinear interpolation. It calculates the proportional
distance of each tree relative to the local field corners and applies those
exact proportions to the projected GPS corners. Because this method forces the
plot's corners to strictly match the averaged GPS coordinates, the internal
geometry of the plot may be warped, meaning the geographic distances between
projected trees may not perfectly match the distances measured in the field.

All points must share one projected coordinate reference system. If plots
span more than one UTM zone, all points are transformed to the most common
zone. `plotPolygonFit()` warns if the fitted transformation is a reflection,
which usually means that the relative coordinates are mirrored, e.g. if X and
Y are swapped.

```{r}
# Points must share one projected CRS. If plots span more than one UTM zone,
# transform all points to the most common zone
crs_site <- as.integer(names(which.max(table(L0$pt$crs_epsg))))
pt_fit <- L0$pt
if (length(unique(pt_fit$crs_epsg)) > 1) {
  for (i in setdiff(unique(pt_fit$crs_epsg), crs_site)) {
    sel <- pt_fit$crs_epsg == i & 
      !is.na(pt_fit$rover_easting_utm_m) & !is.na(pt_fit$rover_northing_utm_m)
    xy <- st_coordinates(st_transform(
      st_as_sf(pt_fit[sel, ], 
        coords = c("rover_easting_utm_m", "rover_northing_utm_m"), crs = i), 
      crs_site))
    pt_fit$rover_easting_utm_m[sel] <- xy[, 1]
    pt_fit$rover_northing_utm_m[sel] <- xy[, 2]
  }
  pt_fit$crs_epsg <- crs_site
}
```

Stems without coordinates in trees where other stems have coordinates are
given the mean coordinates of the other stems of the tree:

```{r}
# Stems without coordinates in trees where other stems have coordinates are
# given the mean coordinates of the other stems of the tree. Trees are 
# identified by `tree_id` within each plot
stem_xy <- L0$stem %>%
  mutate(tree_grp = ifelse(is.na(tree_id) | tree_id == "",
    paste0("record::", record_id), paste(plot_id, tree_id, sep = "::"))) %>%
  group_by(tree_grp) %>%
  mutate(
    xy_ok = !is.na(x_rel_m) & !is.na(y_rel_m),
    xy_from_tree = !xy_ok & any(xy_ok),
    x_rel_m = ifelse(xy_from_tree, mean(x_rel_m[xy_ok]), x_rel_m),
    y_rel_m = ifelse(xy_from_tree, mean(y_rel_m[xy_ok]), y_rel_m)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-tree_grp, -xy_ok)
sum(stem_xy$xy_from_tree)
```

```{r}
# Select only relevant columns from stems dataframe
# Filter to only plots with spatial coordinates
# Multi-stemmed trees are assigned to the quadrat containing the centroid of
# their stems, so `x_quad` and `y_quad` are used to assign quadrats, while
# stem locations are kept
stem_sel <- stem_xy %>%
  left_join(., treeEquiv(stem_xy, tree_include)[, c("record_id", "tree_key")],
    by = "record_id") %>%
  dplyr::select(record_id, plot_id, tree_key, x_rel_m, y_rel_m) %>%
  filter(
    plot_id %in% L0$pt$plot_id,
    !is.na(x_rel_m),
    !is.na(y_rel_m)) %>%
  group_by(tree_key) %>%
  mutate(
    x_quad = mean(x_rel_m),
    y_quad = mean(y_rel_m)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-tree_key)
```

```{r}
# Extract plot corners
plot_check <- BIOMASS::plotPolygonFit(
  point_data = pt_fit,
  method = param$polygon_method,
  rel_col = c("x_rel_m", "y_rel_m"),
  proj_col = c("rover_easting_utm_m", "rover_northing_utm_m"),
  lonlat_col = NULL,
  corner_col = "corner",
  plot_col = "plot_id",
  max_dist = param$corner_outlier_dist_m,
  rm_outliers = TRUE,
  tree_data = if (nrow(stem_sel) > 0) stem_sel else NULL,
  tree_rel_col = c("x_rel_m", "y_rel_m"),
  tree_plot_col = if (nrow(stem_sel) > 0) "plot_id" else NULL,
  raster = NULL,
  shapefile = NULL,
  prop_tree = NULL,
  threshold_tree = NULL, 
  draw_plot = FALSE,
  ask = FALSE)
```

Next we divide the plot into 50x50 m (0.25 ha) quadrats using the
`BIOMASS::divide_plot()` function. This function also assigns stem measurements
to individual quadrats. Where a multi-stemmed tree has stems in more than one
quadrat, all its stems are assigned to the quadrat containing the centroid of
its stems. 

Each plot is divided separately, as `divide_plot()` uses one grid origin for
all plots. The grid is aligned by `quad_origin` in `param.yaml`: `"centre"`
centres the grid in the plot, `"corner"` starts the grid at the origin corner
of the plot, and a pair of numbers `[x, y]` starts the grid `x` and `y` m from
the origin corner. Where the plot dimensions are not a multiple of the quadrat
dimensions, strips along the edges of the plot are left out of the grid, e.g.
with `"centre"`, 25 m strips along each edge of a 250 x 250 m plot divided
into 100 x 100 m quadrats. `grid_tol`, set by `quad_grid_tol` in
`param.yaml`, is the maximum proportion of the plot area which may be left
out of the grid. With `0.1` an error is returned if more than 10% of the plot
area is not covered by the grid of quadrats. In this example the plot
dimensions are a multiple of the quadrat dimensions, so no area is left out.

```{r}
# Divide plots into 50x50 m quadrats, assigning stems to quadrats using the
# centroid of their tree. divide_plot() renames `tree_coords` to `x_rel` and
# `y_rel`, so the stem coordinates are removed
tree_quad <- if (nrow(stem_sel) > 0) {
  dplyr::select(plot_check$tree_data, -x_rel, -y_rel)
} else {
  NULL
}

# Each plot is divided separately, with the quadrat grid aligned by 
# `quad_origin`
corner_coord <- as.data.frame(plot_check$corner_coord)
divide_list <- lapply(split(corner_coord, corner_coord$plot_ID), function(cc) {
  x_rng <- range(cc$x_rel)
  y_rng <- range(cc$y_rel)
  origin <- if (identical(param$quad_origin, "centre")) {
    c(x_rng[1] + (diff(x_rng) %% param$quad_dim[1]) / 2,
      y_rng[1] + (diff(y_rng) %% param$quad_dim[2]) / 2)
  } else if (identical(param$quad_origin, "corner")) {
    c(x_rng[1], y_rng[1])
  } else {
    c(x_rng[1], y_rng[1]) + param$quad_origin
  }
  td <- if (!is.null(tree_quad)) {
    tree_quad[tree_quad$plot_ID == cc$plot_ID[1], , drop = FALSE]
  } else {
    NULL
  }
  if (!is.null(td) && nrow(td) == 0) td <- NULL

  BIOMASS::divide_plot(
    corner_data = cc,
    rel_coord = c("x_rel", "y_rel"),
    proj_coord = c("x_proj", "y_proj"),
    longlat = NULL,
    grid_size = param$quad_dim,
    grid_tol = param$quad_grid_tol,
    origin = origin,
    tree_data = td,
    tree_coords = if (!is.null(td)) c("x_quad", "y_quad") else NULL,
    corner_plot_ID = "plot_ID",
    tree_plot_ID = if (!is.null(td)) "plot_ID" else NULL,
    sd_coord = NULL, 
    n = 100)
})
plot_divide <- list(
  sub_corner_coord = bind_rows(lapply(divide_list, function(x) {
    as.data.frame(x$sub_corner_coord)
  })),
  tree_data = bind_rows(lapply(divide_list, function(x) {
    if (is.null(x$tree_data)) NULL else as.data.frame(x$tree_data)
  })))
```

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Example of output of `BIOMASS::divide_plot()`."
# Inspect output
kable(head(plot_divide$sub_corner_coord))

kable(head(plot_divide$tree_data))
```

Finally, we clean up the outputs of `plotPolygonFit()` and `divide_plot()` and
create `sf` spatial objects. We now have the following objects:

* `plot_poly` - `sf` object with a spatial polygon for each plot.
* `quad_poly` - `sf` object with spatial polygons for each 50x50 m quadrat.
* `stem_pt` - `sf` object with spatial points for each stem measurement.

```{r}
# Stems outside the quadrat grid
# Stems whose tree centroid is outside the quadrat grid, by up to
# `outside_max_dist_m`, are assigned to the nearest quadrat. Others are
# excluded from quadrat summaries. In the automated workflow stems outside
# the plot are written to `report/stem_outside.csv`, so that raw data can be
# corrected if needed. Stems inside the plot, in strips left out of the 
# quadrat grid, are marked with `grid_excl`
if (nrow(stem_sel) > 0) {
  plot_divide$tree_data$grid_excl <- FALSE
  tree_dat <- plot_divide$tree_data
  quad_ext <- plot_divide$sub_corner_coord %>%
    group_by(plot_ID, subplot_ID) %>%
    summarise(
      x_min = min(x_rel), x_max = max(x_rel),
      y_min = min(y_rel), y_max = max(y_rel),
      .groups = "drop")
  plot_ext <- corner_coord %>%
    group_by(plot_ID) %>%
    summarise(
      x_min = min(x_rel), x_max = max(x_rel),
      y_min = min(y_rel), y_max = max(y_rel),
      .groups = "drop")

  # Distance from tree centroid to nearest quadrat. `x_rel` and `y_rel` in
  # the output of divide_plot() are the tree centroid
  out_idx <- which(is.na(tree_dat$subplot_ID))
  quad_near <- lapply(out_idx, function(i) {
    q <- quad_ext[quad_ext$plot_ID == tree_dat$plot_ID[i], ]
    d <- sqrt(
      pmax(q$x_min - tree_dat$x_rel[i], 0, tree_dat$x_rel[i] - q$x_max)^2 +
      pmax(q$y_min - tree_dat$y_rel[i], 0, tree_dat$y_rel[i] - q$y_max)^2)
    data.frame(quadrat_nearest = q$subplot_ID[which.min(d)], dist_m = min(d))
  })
  quad_near <- bind_rows(quad_near,
    data.frame(quadrat_nearest = character(0), dist_m = numeric(0)))

  # Whether the tree centroid is inside the plot
  pe <- plot_ext[match(tree_dat$plot_ID[out_idx], plot_ext$plot_ID), ]
  in_plot <- tree_dat$x_rel[out_idx] >= pe$x_min & 
    tree_dat$x_rel[out_idx] <= pe$x_max &
    tree_dat$y_rel[out_idx] >= pe$y_min & 
    tree_dat$y_rel[out_idx] <= pe$y_max

  stem_outside <- data.frame(
    record_id = tree_dat$record_id[out_idx],
    quadrat_nearest = quad_near$quadrat_nearest,
    dist_m = round(quad_near$dist_m, 2)) %>%
    mutate(
      action = case_when(
        dist_m <= param$outside_max_dist_m ~ "assigned to nearest quadrat",
        in_plot ~ "excluded, in plot outside quadrat grid",
        TRUE ~ "excluded"))

  # Assign stems to nearest quadrat
  assign_idx <- out_idx[stem_outside$action == "assigned to nearest quadrat"]
  plot_divide$tree_data$subplot_ID[assign_idx] <- stem_outside$quadrat_nearest[
    stem_outside$action == "assigned to nearest quadrat"]

  # Mark stems in strips left out of the quadrat grid
  grid_excl_idx <- out_idx[stem_outside$action == "excluded, in plot outside quadrat grid"]
  plot_divide$tree_data$grid_excl[grid_excl_idx] <- TRUE
  stem_outside <- filter(stem_outside, action != "excluded, in plot outside quadrat grid")

  # Stems outside the quadrat grid, to check raw data
  stem_outside <- stem_xy %>%
    dplyr::select(record_id, plot_id, tree_id, stem_id, x_rel_m, y_rel_m,
      diam_cm, code) %>%
    inner_join(., stem_outside, by = "record_id") %>%
    arrange(desc(dist_m))
}

# Create plot polygons 
plot_poly <- plot_check$polygon %>% 
  rename(plot_id = plot_ID) %>% 
  st_set_crs(crs_site) %>% 
  mutate(    
    site_id = param$site_id,
    acquisition_id = param$acquisition_id, 
    .before = everything())

# Create quadrat corner spatial points
quad_pt <- plot_divide$sub_corner_coord %>% 
  mutate(
    x_utm = x_proj,
    y_utm = y_proj) %>% 
  st_as_sf(., coords = c("x_proj", "y_proj"), crs = crs_site) %>% 
  mutate(    
    site_id = param$site_id,
    acquisition_id = param$acquisition_id, 
    .before = everything()) %>% 
  rename(
    plot_id = plot_ID, 
    quadrat_id = subplot_ID,
    x_rel_m = x_rel,
    y_rel_m = y_rel)

# Create quadrat polygons
quad_poly <- quad_pt %>% 
  group_by(site_id, acquisition_id, plot_id, quadrat_id) %>%
  summarise() %>% 
  st_convex_hull() %>%
  ungroup()

# Create stem spatial points
# Stems without coordinates are not included
if (nrow(stem_sel) > 0) {
  stem_pt <- plot_divide$tree_data %>%
    mutate(
      x_utm = x_proj,
      y_utm = y_proj) %>%
    filter(!is.na(x_proj), !is.na(y_proj)) %>%
    st_as_sf(., coords = c("x_proj", "y_proj"), crs = crs_site) %>%
    mutate(xy_from_tree = stem_xy$xy_from_tree[match(record_id, stem_xy$record_id)]) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      record_id,
      quadrat_id = subplot_ID,
      grid_excl,
      xy_from_tree,
      x_utm, y_utm)
} else {
  stem_pt <- st_sf(
    record_id = integer(0),
    quadrat_id = character(0),
    grid_excl = logical(0),
    xy_from_tree = logical(0),
    x_utm = numeric(0),
    y_utm = numeric(0),
    geometry = st_sfc(crs = crs_site))
}
```

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Example of quadrat polygons object`."
kable(head(quad_poly))
```

We summarise the fitted plot polygons. The area of the fitted polygon should
be close to the area defined by the relative coordinates of the plot corners.
A large difference suggests errors in the corner coordinates.
`grid_excl_pct` is the percentage of the plot area left out of the quadrat
grid. In the automated workflow this table is written to
`07_quad/plot_poly_check.csv`.

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Fitted plot polygons, compared to the area defined by the relative coordinates of the plot corners."
# Summarise plot polygons. The area of the fitted polygon should be close to
# the area defined by the relative coordinates of the plot corners. A large
# difference suggests errors in the corner coordinates. `grid_excl_pct` is 
# the percentage of the plot area left out of the quadrat grid
corner_rel <- pt_fit %>%
  filter(corner %in% TRUE) %>%
  distinct(plot_id, x_rel_m, y_rel_m)
area_rel <- vapply(split(corner_rel, corner_rel$plot_id), function(x) {
  as.numeric(st_area(st_convex_hull(st_multipoint(
    as.matrix(x[, c("x_rel_m", "y_rel_m")]))))) / 10000
}, numeric(1))

outliers <- if (is.null(plot_check$outliers)) {
  data.frame(plot_ID = character(0), x_proj = numeric(0), y_proj = numeric(0))
} else {
  plot_check$outliers
}

poly_check <- data.frame(
  plot_id = as.character(plot_poly$plot_id),
  area_ha_poly = as.numeric(st_area(plot_poly)) / 10000) %>%
  mutate(
    area_ha_rel = unname(area_rel[plot_id]),
    area_diff_pct = round(100 * (area_ha_poly - area_ha_rel) / area_ha_rel, 1),
    n_gnss = as.vector(table(pt_fit$plot_id)[plot_id]),
    n_gnss_outlier = as.vector(table(factor(outliers$plot_ID, levels = plot_id))),
    n_quadrat = as.vector(table(factor(quad_poly$plot_id, levels = plot_id))),
    area_ha_quad = as.vector(tapply(as.numeric(st_area(quad_poly)) / 10000,
      factor(quad_poly$plot_id, levels = plot_id), sum)),
    grid_excl_pct = round(100 * (1 - area_ha_quad / area_ha_poly), 1)) %>%
  arrange(plotFactor(plot_id))
if (nrow(stem_sel) > 0) {
  stem_grid_excl <- stem_sel$plot_id[stem_sel$record_id %in% 
    plot_divide$tree_data$record_id[plot_divide$tree_data$grid_excl]]
  poly_check <- poly_check %>%
    mutate(
      n_stem_mapped = as.vector(table(factor(stem_sel$plot_id, levels = plot_id))),
      n_stem_outside = as.vector(table(factor(stem_outside$plot_id, levels = plot_id))),
      n_stem_grid_excl = as.vector(table(factor(stem_grid_excl, levels = plot_id))))
}

if (any(abs(poly_check$area_diff_pct) > 5, na.rm = TRUE)) {
  warning("Fitted polygon area differs from the area defined by the plot ",
    "corners by more than 5% in plots: ", 
    paste(poly_check$plot_id[abs(poly_check$area_diff_pct) > 5], collapse = ", "),
    ". Check plot corner coordinates, see ", 
    file.path(report_dir, "07_plot_poly.png"), call. = FALSE)
}

kable(poly_check)
```

Stems outside the quadrat grid are written to `report/stem_outside.csv` by
the automated workflow, so that raw data can be corrected if needed.

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Fitted plot polygons, outlines of the GNSS corners, quadrats, and GNSS points, including outliers removed during polygon fitting."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
# Figure of plot polygons, quadrats and GNSS points. Coordinates are 
# relative to the south-west corner of the bounding box of each plot, so that
# plots can be shown side by side at the same scale
plot_xy <- polyCoords(plot_poly, "plot_id")
quad_xy <- polyCoords(quad_poly, "plot_id")
plot_origin <- plot_xy %>%
  group_by(plot_id) %>%
  summarise(x0 = min(X), y0 = min(Y), .groups = "drop")

gnss_xy <- pt_fit %>%
  filter(!is.na(rover_easting_utm_m), !is.na(rover_northing_utm_m)) %>%
  transmute(
    plot_id = as.character(plot_id), 
    X = rover_easting_utm_m, 
    Y = rover_northing_utm_m,
    type = ifelse(corner %in% TRUE, "GNSS point, corner", "GNSS point, other"))
outlier_xy <- transmute(outliers, plot_id = as.character(plot_ID), X = x_proj, 
  Y = y_proj, type = "Outlier, removed")
pt_xy <- bind_rows(gnss_xy, outlier_xy)

# Outline of the GNSS corners of each plot, from the mean of repeated
# measurements of each corner, ordered around the plot
corner_raw <- pt_fit %>%
  filter(corner %in% TRUE, !is.na(rover_easting_utm_m), 
    !is.na(rover_northing_utm_m)) %>%
  mutate(plot_id = as.character(plot_id)) %>%
  group_by(plot_id, x_rel_m, y_rel_m) %>%
  summarise(X = mean(rover_easting_utm_m), Y = mean(rover_northing_utm_m), 
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(plot_id) %>%
  filter(n() >= 3) %>%
  mutate(angle = atan2(y_rel_m - mean(y_rel_m), x_rel_m - mean(x_rel_m))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(plot_id, angle) %>%
  mutate(group = plot_id)

pt_type <- c(
  "GNSS point, corner" = fig_pal$series[1], 
  "GNSS point, other" = fig_pal$series[2],
  "Outlier, removed" = fig_pal$problem)
pt_type <- pt_type[names(pt_type) %in% pt_xy$type]

p_poly <- ggplot() +
  # Wider than the fitted polygon, so that it is visible where they overlap
  geom_polygon(data = localXY(corner_raw, "X", "Y", "plot_id", plot_origin),
    aes(x = X, y = Y, group = group), 
    fill = NA, colour = fig_pal$series[1], linewidth = 1.4) +
  geom_polygon(data = localXY(quad_xy, "X", "Y", "plot_id", plot_origin),
    aes(x = X, y = Y, group = group), 
    fill = NA, colour = fig_pal$line_muted, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_polygon(data = localXY(plot_xy, "X", "Y", "plot_id", plot_origin),
    aes(x = X, y = Y, group = group), 
    fill = NA, colour = fig_pal$ink, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = localXY(pt_xy, "X", "Y", "plot_id", plot_origin),
    aes(x = X, y = Y, colour = type, shape = type), size = 3.5, stroke = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(NULL, values = pt_type, breaks = names(pt_type)) +
  scale_shape_manual(NULL, values = c("GNSS point, corner" = 16, 
    "GNSS point, other" = 16, "Outlier, removed" = 4)[names(pt_type)],
    breaks = names(pt_type)) +
  facet_wrap(vars(plotFactor(plot_id)), ncol = figCols(nrow(plot_origin))) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = "Plot polygons, quadrats and GNSS points",
    x = "Easting (m)",
    y = "Northing (m)") +
  themeMap()
p_poly
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Stem locations within the quadrat grid of each plot, with plot outlines, highlighting stems outside the plot, and stems in strips left out of the quadrat grid."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
# Figure of stem locations within the quadrat grid, in plot coordinates
if (nrow(stem_sel) > 0) {
  quad_rel <- plot_divide$sub_corner_coord %>%
    group_by(plot_id = as.character(plot_ID), subplot_ID) %>%
    summarise(
      x_min = min(x_rel), x_max = max(x_rel),
      y_min = min(y_rel), y_max = max(y_rel),
      .groups = "drop")

  stem_map_rel <- stem_sel %>%
    mutate(plot_id = as.character(plot_id)) %>%
    left_join(., dplyr::select(stem_outside, record_id, action), 
      by = "record_id") %>%
    left_join(., dplyr::select(plot_divide$tree_data, record_id, grid_excl),
      by = "record_id") %>%
    mutate(type = case_when(
      grid_excl %in% TRUE ~ "In plot, left out of quadrat grid",
      is.na(action) ~ "Stem, in quadrat grid",
      action == "excluded" ~ "Outside grid, excluded",
      TRUE ~ "Outside grid, assigned to nearest quadrat"))

  stem_type <- c(
    "Stem, in quadrat grid" = fig_pal$series[1],
    "In plot, left out of quadrat grid" = fig_pal$line_muted,
    "Outside grid, assigned to nearest quadrat" = fig_pal$warn,
    "Outside grid, excluded" = fig_pal$problem)
  stem_type <- stem_type[names(stem_type) %in% stem_map_rel$type]
  stem_in_plot <- c("Stem, in quadrat grid", "In plot, left out of quadrat grid")
  n_plot_stem <- length(unique(stem_map_rel$plot_id))

  # Stems far outside the quadrat grid, e.g. with coordinate errors, are
  # shown at the edge of the map, so that plots are large enough to see
  map_x <- range(c(quad_rel$x_min, quad_rel$x_max, plot_ext$x_min, plot_ext$x_max))
  map_y <- range(c(quad_rel$y_min, quad_rel$y_max, plot_ext$y_min, plot_ext$y_max))
  map_margin <- 0.1 * max(diff(map_x), diff(map_y))
  map_x <- map_x + c(-1, 1) * map_margin
  map_y <- map_y + c(-1, 1) * map_margin
  stem_map_rel <- stem_map_rel %>%
    mutate(
      edge = ifelse(x_rel_m < map_x[1] | x_rel_m > map_x[2] | 
        y_rel_m < map_y[1] | y_rel_m > map_y[2], 
        "Beyond map edge, shown at edge", "Within map"),
      # Inset from the edge, so that points are not clipped
      x_rel_m = pmin(pmax(x_rel_m, map_x[1] + 0.25 * map_margin), 
        map_x[2] - 0.25 * map_margin),
      y_rel_m = pmin(pmax(y_rel_m, map_y[1] + 0.25 * map_margin), 
        map_y[2] - 0.25 * map_margin))

  p_stem <- ggplot() +
    geom_rect(data = filter(quad_rel, plot_id %in% stem_map_rel$plot_id),
      aes(xmin = x_min, xmax = x_max, ymin = y_min, ymax = y_max),
      fill = NA, colour = fig_pal$line_muted, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_rect(data = filter(mutate(plot_ext, plot_id = as.character(plot_ID)), 
      plot_id %in% stem_map_rel$plot_id),
      aes(xmin = x_min, xmax = x_max, ymin = y_min, ymax = y_max),
      fill = NA, colour = fig_pal$ink, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_point(data = filter(stem_map_rel, type %in% stem_in_plot),
      aes(x = x_rel_m, y = y_rel_m, colour = type), 
      size = 0.8, alpha = 0.7, shape = 16) +
    scale_colour_manual(NULL, values = stem_type, breaks = names(stem_type)) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(order = 1,
      override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1, shape = 16)))
  # Stems outside the plot, only if there are any, as an empty layer gives a
  # warning from the shape scale
  if (any(!stem_map_rel$type %in% stem_in_plot)) {
    p_stem <- p_stem +
      geom_point(data = filter(stem_map_rel, !type %in% stem_in_plot),
        aes(x = x_rel_m, y = y_rel_m, colour = type, shape = edge), size = 2.4) +
      scale_shape_manual(NULL, values = c("Within map" = 16,
        "Beyond map edge, shown at edge" = 17),
        breaks = intersect("Beyond map edge, shown at edge", stem_map_rel$edge)) +
      guides(shape = guide_legend(order = 2,
        override.aes = list(size = 2, colour = fig_pal$ink_muted)))
  }
  p_stem <- p_stem +
    facet_wrap(vars(plotFactor(plot_id)), ncol = figCols(n_plot_stem)) +
    coord_equal(xlim = map_x, ylim = map_y, expand = FALSE) +
    labs(
      title = "Stem locations and quadrats",
      x = "X (m)",
      y = "Y (m)") +
    themeMap()
  print(p_stem)
}
```

Where the site supplies the bounds of field subplots, in the optional subplot
table, stems are checked against the bounds of their field subplot. Stems
outside them are written to `report/stem_outside_subplot.csv` by the
automated workflow, as either the coordinates or the field subplot of the
stem may be wrong. The bounds are also used to place trees without
coordinates, see [Estimate quadrat AGBD and propagate error]. The field
subplots of the example data are 20x20 m.

```{r}
subplot <- mutate(L0$subplot, plot_id = as.character(plot_id))

# Stems with a field subplot. Stems given the coordinates of their tree are
# not checked
stem_sub <- stem_xy %>%
  filter(!is.na(subplot_id), subplot_id != "") %>%
  mutate(plot_id = as.character(plot_id)) %>%
  left_join(., dplyr::select(subplot, plot_id, subplot_id, x_rel_min_m, 
    x_rel_max_m, y_rel_min_m, y_rel_max_m), by = c("plot_id", "subplot_id")) %>%
  mutate(
    mapped = !is.na(x_rel_m) & !is.na(y_rel_m) & !xy_from_tree,
    in_table = !is.na(x_rel_min_m),
    # Distance from the stem to the nearest edge of its field subplot
    dist_m = sqrt(
      pmax(x_rel_min_m - x_rel_m, 0, x_rel_m - x_rel_max_m)^2 +
      pmax(y_rel_min_m - y_rel_m, 0, y_rel_m - y_rel_max_m)^2),
    inside = mapped & in_table & dist_m == 0)

# Stems outside the bounds of their field subplot, with the field subplot
# whose bounds contain them, if any
stem_outside_sub <- filter(stem_sub, mapped, !inside)
stem_outside_sub$subplot_id_contain <- mapply(function(p, x, y) {
  i <- which(subplot$plot_id == p & 
    x >= subplot$x_rel_min_m & x <= subplot$x_rel_max_m &
    y >= subplot$y_rel_min_m & y <= subplot$y_rel_max_m)
  if (length(i) == 0) NA_character_ else subplot$subplot_id[i[1]]
}, stem_outside_sub$plot_id, stem_outside_sub$x_rel_m, 
  stem_outside_sub$y_rel_m, USE.NAMES = FALSE)
stem_outside_sub <- stem_outside_sub %>%
  transmute(record_id, plot_id, tree_id, stem_id, subplot_id, x_rel_m, 
    y_rel_m, diam_cm, code, x_rel_min_m, x_rel_max_m, y_rel_min_m, 
    y_rel_max_m, dist_m = round(dist_m, 2), 
    subplot_id_contain = as.character(subplot_id_contain),
    issue = ifelse(in_table, "outside subplot bounds", 
      "subplot not in subplot table")) %>%
  arrange(plotFactor(plot_id), desc(dist_m))

if (nrow(stem_outside_sub) > 0) {
  message(sum(stem_outside_sub$issue == "outside subplot bounds"), 
    " stems with coordinates outside the bounds of their field subplot, and ",
    sum(stem_outside_sub$issue != "outside subplot bounds"), 
    " stems in field subplots not in the subplot table. See ",
    file.path(report_dir, "stem_outside_subplot.csv"))
}
```

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Stems with coordinates outside the bounds of their field subplot, with their distance to the nearest edge of the subplot, and the field subplot whose bounds contain them, if any."
kable(head(stem_outside_sub, 10))
```

We summarise each field subplot, and each plot. `pct_in` is the percentage
of stems with coordinates within the bounds of their subplot, and
`pct_in_min` the lowest of any subplot in the plot. In the automated
workflow the summary of each field subplot is written to
`07_quad/subplot_check.csv`.

```{r}
# Summarise each field subplot. Stems without coordinates are those of 
# trees where no stems have coordinates
subplot_check <- subplot %>%
  dplyr::select(plot_id, subplot_id, x_rel_min_m, x_rel_max_m, y_rel_min_m,
    y_rel_max_m) %>%
  left_join(., stem_sub %>%
    group_by(plot_id, subplot_id) %>%
    summarise(
      n_stem_mapped = sum(mapped),
      n_stem_outside = sum(mapped & !inside),
      n_stem_unmapped = sum(is.na(x_rel_m) | is.na(y_rel_m)),
      .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("plot_id", "subplot_id")) %>%
  mutate(
    across(starts_with("n_stem"), ~ifelse(is.na(.x), 0L, .x)),
    dim_x_m = x_rel_max_m - x_rel_min_m,
    dim_y_m = y_rel_max_m - y_rel_min_m,
    pct_in = round(100 * (1 - n_stem_outside / n_stem_mapped), 1)) %>%
  arrange(plotFactor(plot_id), suppressWarnings(as.numeric(subplot_id)), 
    subplot_id)
```

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Field subplots in each plot, from the subplot table."
subplot_plot <- subplot_check %>%
  group_by(plot_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_subplot = n(),
    subplot_dim_m = paste(unique(paste(dim_x_m, "x", dim_y_m)), 
      collapse = ", "),
    pct_in_min = suppressWarnings(min(pct_in, na.rm = TRUE)),
    n_stem_mapped = sum(n_stem_mapped),
    n_stem_outside = sum(n_stem_outside),
    pct_in = round(100 * (1 - n_stem_outside / n_stem_mapped), 1),
    n_stem_unmapped = sum(n_stem_unmapped),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(pct_in_min = ifelse(is.infinite(pct_in_min), NA, pct_in_min)) %>%
  arrange(plotFactor(plot_id))

kable(subplot_plot)
```

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Field subplots where fewer than 90% of stems are within the bounds."
kable(dplyr::select(filter(subplot_check, pct_in < 90), plot_id, subplot_id,
  x_rel_min_m, x_rel_max_m, y_rel_min_m, y_rel_max_m, n_stem_mapped, pct_in))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Field subplots in each plot, labelled with their ID and filled by the percentage of stems with coordinates outside their bounds. Stems outside their subplot are shown in red, joined to the nearest edge of their subplot. Stems far outside are shown at the edge of the map. Subplots without stems with coordinates are grey."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
# Figure of field subplots in each plot, filled by the percentage of stems
# outside their bounds, with stems outside joined to the nearest edge of
# their subplot. Stems far outside the subplots of their plot, e.g. with 
# coordinate errors, are shown at the edge of the map
sub_fig <- subplot_check %>%
  filter(n_stem_mapped > 0) %>%
  mutate(pct_out = 100 - pct_in)
if (nrow(sub_fig) > 0) {
  sub_fig <- filter(subplot_check, plot_id %in% sub_fig$plot_id) %>%
    mutate(
      pct_out = 100 - pct_in,
      x_mid = (x_rel_min_m + x_rel_max_m) / 2,
      y_mid = (y_rel_min_m + y_rel_max_m) / 2)
  # Map extent includes the plot corners, as the subplot table may not
  # cover the whole plot
  sub_ext <- bind_rows(
    dplyr::select(sub_fig, plot_id, x_rel_min_m, x_rel_max_m, y_rel_min_m, 
      y_rel_max_m),
    corner_rel %>%
      filter(plot_id %in% sub_fig$plot_id) %>%
      transmute(plot_id = as.character(plot_id), x_rel_min_m = x_rel_m, 
        x_rel_max_m = x_rel_m, y_rel_min_m = y_rel_m, 
        y_rel_max_m = y_rel_m)) %>%
    group_by(plot_id) %>%
    summarise(
      x0 = min(x_rel_min_m), x1 = max(x_rel_max_m),
      y0 = min(y_rel_min_m), y1 = max(y_rel_max_m),
      .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(m = 0.1 * pmax(x1 - x0, y1 - y0))
  sub_extent <- with(sub_ext, data.frame(
    plot_id = rep(plot_id, 2),
    x = c(x0 - m, x1 + m),
    y = c(y0 - m, y1 + m)))
  out_fig <- stem_outside_sub %>%
    filter(issue == "outside subplot bounds", plot_id %in% sub_fig$plot_id) %>%
    left_join(., sub_ext, by = "plot_id") %>%
    mutate(
      x_rel_m = pmin(pmax(x_rel_m, x0 - 0.75 * m), x1 + 0.75 * m),
      y_rel_m = pmin(pmax(y_rel_m, y0 - 0.75 * m), y1 + 0.75 * m),
      x_edge = pmin(pmax(x_rel_m, x_rel_min_m), x_rel_max_m),
      y_edge = pmin(pmax(y_rel_m, y_rel_min_m), y_rel_max_m))
  n_plot_sub <- nrow(sub_ext)
  # Labels are light on the darkest fills
  pct_out_lim <- c(0, max(c(sub_fig$pct_out, 1), na.rm = TRUE))
  sub_fig$label_colour <- ifelse(sub_fig$pct_out %in% NA | 
    sub_fig$pct_out < 0.6 * pct_out_lim[2], fig_pal$ink, fig_pal$surface)
  # Labels are smaller in plots with many subplots, so that they fit
  sub_label_size <- min(3.2, 32 / sqrt(max(table(sub_fig$plot_id))))

  p_sub <- ggplot() +
    geom_blank(data = squareExtent(sub_extent, "x", "y", "plot_id"),
      aes(x = x, y = y)) +
    geom_rect(data = sub_fig,
      aes(xmin = x_rel_min_m, xmax = x_rel_max_m, ymin = y_rel_min_m, 
        ymax = y_rel_max_m, fill = pct_out),
      colour = fig_pal$surface, linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_gradientn("Stems outside the bounds of their subplot (%)",
      colours = fig_pal$seq, limits = pct_out_lim, na.value = fig_pal$grid,
      guide = colourBar()) +
    geom_segment(data = out_fig, 
      aes(x = x_rel_m, y = y_rel_m, xend = x_edge, yend = y_edge),
      colour = fig_pal$problem, linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_point(data = out_fig, aes(x = x_rel_m, y = y_rel_m), 
      colour = fig_pal$problem, size = 0.9, shape = 16) +
    geom_text(data = sub_fig, 
      aes(x = x_mid, y = y_mid, label = subplot_id, colour = label_colour),
      size = sub_label_size) +
    scale_colour_identity() +
    facet_wrap(vars(plotFactor(plot_id)), ncol = figCols(n_plot_sub),
      scales = "free") +
    labs(
      title = "Field subplots",
      x = "X (m)",
      y = "Y (m)") +
    themeMap() +
    theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
  print(p_sub)
}
```

## Estimate quadrat AGBD and propagate error

`08_agb_mc.R`

Here we estimate the above-ground woody biomass density (AGBD) in each 50x50 m
quadrat, with its uncertainty. The `BIOMASS::AGBmonteCarlo()` function
propagates errors in stem diameter, wood density, height, and the AGB
allometry to each stem, using Monte-Carlo simulation. The
`BIOMASS::subplot_summary()` function then sums the simulated AGB of the stems
in each quadrat and divides by the quadrat area, giving a distribution of 1000
simulated AGBD values for each quadrat.

The errors propagated depend on `height_method`:

* `"regional"` - Equation 7 from @Chave2014 is used, with the uncertainty in
  the environmental stress index (E) and the model parameters. Stem height is
  not used.
* `"field"` - Equation 4 from @Chave2014 is used, with stem height predicted
  from the local height-diameter model, including its uncertainty.
* `"custom"` - Equation 4 from @Chave2014 is used, with stem height predicted
  from the height-diameter model in `height_custom`, including its residual
  error.

If `stem_allometry` is `true`, trees with another allometry in
`agb_allometry`, see [Estimate stem AGB], are simulated separately, with the
residual error of their allometry, by passing the allometry to the
`fitted_allom` argument of `AGBmonteCarlo()`. Diameters are corrected for
taper if `taper_method` is set, see [Estimate stem height].

As in [Estimate stem AGB], AGB is simulated for each multi-stemmed tree from
its equivalent diameter, then shared among its stems in proportion to their
basal area.

`AGBmonteCarlo()` is run on groups of whole plots, or groups of whole quadrats
for very large plots, rather than on each quadrat separately. This means that
quadrats containing a single tree get an uncertainty estimate, that the large
diameter errors of @Chave2004, applied to 5% of stems, are applied to a
meaningful number of stems, and that stems outside the quadrat grid still get
a stem-level uncertainty estimate.

`subplot_summary()` is run separately for each plot, because when plots have
different numbers of quadrats and a quadrat contains no stems,
`subplot_summary()` can assign AGBD = 0 to quadrats which contain stems.

Stems without a diameter have their diameter imputed in each simulation by
`AGBmonteCarlo()`, from the simulated diameters of the other trees in the
same call, i.e. the same plot and AGB allometry, which can include trees below the minimum
diameter threshold for AGBD. For very large plots, split into groups of
quadrats, the trees in the same group of quadrats are used.

Trees where no stems have coordinates are placed at a random location in each
simulation by `subplot_summary()`, within bounds given by `tree_bounds`, and
their AGB is added to the quadrat containing that location. The bounds are
those of the field subplot of the tree, from the optional subplot table, or,
if the site does not supply it, from the extent of the stems with coordinates
in the same field subplot, if there are at least 10 of them, otherwise those
of the plot. Placements in strips of the plot left out of the quadrat grid
are not included in that simulation. This adds the uncertainty in their
location to the quadrat AGBD estimates. A plot where no stems have
coordinates gives a similar AGBD in every quadrat, with a wider confidence
interval.

A random seed is set so that the results are reproducible.

First we prepare the input dataset:

```{r}
# Define number of simulations
nsim <- 1000

# Set random seed, so results are reproducible
set.seed(42)

# Define maximum number of trees per AGBmonteCarlo() call, to limit memory use
mc_stems_max <- 10000

# Filter stem data and add quadrat IDs. Diameters are corrected for taper,
# see `taper_method`
stem_fil <- stem_taper %>% 
  filter(record_id %in% record_fil) %>% 
  left_join(., stem_wd_all, by = "record_id") %>% 
  left_join(., stem_height_all, by = "record_id") %>% 
  left_join(., st_drop_geometry(stem_pt)[, c("record_id", "quadrat_id", "grid_excl")], 
    by = "record_id")

if (param$height_method == "regional") {
  stem_fil <- left_join(stem_fil, p_cent, by = "plot_id")
  stopifnot(all(!is.na(stem_fil$X)))
}

# Missing wood density uncertainty would cause stems to be silently dropped
# from simulated AGB sums
stopifnot(all(!is.na(stem_fil$meanWD) & !is.na(stem_fil$sdWD)))

# Equivalent diameter of multi-stemmed trees
stem_fil <- left_join(stem_fil, treeEquiv(stem_fil, tree_include),
  by = "record_id")

# Stems of a tree share the quadrat of the tree. Stems without coordinates in
# trees with other stems that have coordinates are assigned to the quadrat of
# the tree. Trees where no stems have coordinates are assigned to quadrats at
# random below
stem_fil <- stem_fil %>%
  group_by(tree_key) %>%
  mutate(
    # Stems with coordinates, including stems given the mean coordinates of
    # the other stems of their tree
    tree_mapped = any(record_id %in% stem_pt$record_id),
    quadrat_id = first(na.omit(quadrat_id)),
    # In a strip of the plot left out of the quadrat grid
    grid_excl = any(grid_excl %in% TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

# One row per tree. Wood density depends on taxonomic identity, which is the
# same for all stems of a tree, so the wood density of the largest stem is used
tree <- stem_fil %>%
  arrange(desc(ba_share)) %>%
  group_by(tree_key) %>%
  summarise(
    plot_id = first(plot_id),
    quadrat_id = first(quadrat_id),
    diam_eq_cm = first(diam_eq_cm),
    meanWD = first(meanWD),
    sdWD = first(sdWD),
    agb_allometry = if (param$stem_allometry) first(agb_allometry) else NA_character_,
    across(any_of(c("X", "Y")), first),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(agb_allometry = coalesce(na_if(agb_allometry, ""), "chave2014"))

# Group trees into Monte Carlo chunks
# Whole plots, split into groups of whole quadrats for very large plots
quad_chunk <- tree %>%
  count(plot_id, quadrat_id) %>%
  group_by(plot_id) %>%
  mutate(mc_chunk = (cumsum(n) - 1) %/% mc_stems_max) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(plot_id, quadrat_id, mc_chunk)

tree <- left_join(tree, quad_chunk, by = c("plot_id", "quadrat_id"))

tree_split <- split(tree, list(tree$plot_id, tree$mc_chunk), drop = TRUE)
```

Then we run the Monte-Carlo error propagation on each group of trees, and
share the simulated AGB of each tree among its stems:

If repeat diameter measurements of some stems are available, a
site-specific model of diameter measurement error can be estimated with
`BIOMASS::fitDiamError()` and used instead of the model of Chave et al.
(2004). The automated workflow does this if `diam_error` is `"field"`, see
`08_agb_mc.R`. The example data have no repeat measurements, so we use the
value of `diam_error` directly.

```{r}
# Diameter measurement error, see `diam_error` in param.yaml
diam_error <- if (identical(param$diam_error, "none")) NULL else param$diam_error

# Simulate AGB of trees `x` which share the AGB allometry `allom`, see
# `agb_allometries` in func.R. Returns a matrix of trees x simulations
mcTrees <- function(x, allom) {
  # Trees without a diameter can't be imputed if no other trees have a
  # diameter, so they are not included in AGB density
  n_tree <- nrow(x)
  if (all(is.na(x$diam_eq_cm))) {
    return(matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_tree, ncol = nsim))
  }

  # AGBmonteCarlo() fails with a single tree, so duplicate the row and keep
  # the first. Each row of `AGB_simu` is simulated independently
  if (n_tree == 1) {
    x <- x[c(1, 1), ]
  }

  # AGBmonteCarlo() warns where missing diameters are imputed. Allometries 
  # other than Chave et al. (2014) use the heights of the height-diameter 
  # model, if any
  out <- withCallingHandlers(AGBmonteCarlo(
    D = x$diam_eq_cm,
    WD = x$meanWD,
    errWD = x$sdWD,
    H = NULL,
    errH = NULL,
    HDmodel = if (param$height_method %in% c("field", "custom")) height_mod else NULL,
    coord = if (param$height_method == "regional" && allom == "chave2014") {
      as.matrix(x[, c("X", "Y")])
    } else NULL,
    Dpropag = diam_error,
    n = nsim,
    Carbon = FALSE,
    Dlim = NULL,
    fitted_allom = if (allom == "chave2014") {
      "chave2014"
    } else {
      agb_allometries[[allom]][c("formula", "parameters", "link")]
    }),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("NA values in D", conditionMessage(w))) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    })

  out$AGB_simu[seq_len(n_tree), , drop = FALSE]
}

# Run AGB Monte Carlo error propagation on each chunk, separately for each AGB
# allometry. Missing diameters are imputed from the other trees in the same
# chunk with the same allometry
tree_simu_list <- lapply(seq_along(tree_split), function(i) {
  x <- tree_split[[i]]
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(x), ncol = nsim)
  for (a in unique(x$agb_allometry)) {
    rows <- which(x$agb_allometry == a)
    out[rows, ] <- mcTrees(x[rows, ], a)
  }
  out
})

# Combine simulations, then share tree AGB among stems. Rows match `stem_fil`
tree <- bind_rows(tree_split)
tree_simu <- do.call(rbind, tree_simu_list)
stopifnot(nrow(tree_simu) == nrow(tree))
agb_simu <- tree_simu[match(stem_fil$tree_key, tree$tree_key), , drop = FALSE] *
  stem_fil$ba_share

# Trees where no stems have coordinates
unmapped <- !stem_fil$tree_mapped

# Stems below the minimum diameter threshold of the plot are used to estimate
# AGB, but are not included in AGB density
in_agbd <- stem_fil$record_id %in% record_agbd

# Calculate mean and standard deviation of stem AGB
# Stems used to estimate quadrat AGB density are those in a quadrat, and 
# stems of trees without coordinates if they are placed at random. Stems
# without a diameter which could not be imputed are not included
agb_Mg_mean <- rowMeans(agb_simu, na.rm = TRUE)
# Trees without a diameter
tree_imp <- tree$tree_key[is.na(tree$diam_eq_cm)]
stem_agb_mc <- data.frame(
  record_id = stem_fil$record_id,
  agb_Mg_mean = agb_Mg_mean,
  agb_Mg_sd = sqrt(rowSums((agb_simu - agb_Mg_mean)^2, na.rm = TRUE) / 
    (rowSums(!is.na(agb_simu)) - 1)),
  quadrat_id_tree = stem_fil$quadrat_id,
  diam_imputed = stem_fil$tree_key %in% tree_imp & is.finite(agb_Mg_mean),
  in_quadrat_calc = in_agbd & is.finite(agb_Mg_mean) &
    ((!unmapped & !is.na(stem_fil$quadrat_id)) |
    (unmapped & param$unmapped_method == "random")))
```

Stems with imputed diameters are written to `report/diam_imputed.csv` by the
automated workflow, to check raw data.

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Stems without a diameter, imputed from the other trees in the same plot."
diam_imputed <- stem_fil %>%
  filter(record_id %in% stem_agb_mc$record_id[stem_agb_mc$diam_imputed]) %>%
  mutate(agb_Mg_mean = agb_Mg_mean[match(record_id, stem_agb_mc$record_id)]) %>%
  dplyr::select(record_id, plot_id, tree_id, stem_id, taxon_name, code, 
    agb_Mg_mean) %>%
  arrange(plot_id, tree_id, stem_id)

kable(diam_imputed, digits = 3)
```

Then we aggregate the simulations to quadrats:

```{r}
# Format quadrat corner points
quad_pt_clean <- quad_pt %>% 
  st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  dplyr::select(
    plot_ID = plot_id,
    subplot_ID = quadrat_id,
    x_rel = x_rel_m,
    y_rel = y_rel_m,
    x_proj = x_utm,
    y_proj = y_utm)

# Area of each quadrat, from its corners in the order given by divide_plot(),
# as calculated by subplot_summary()
quad_area <- quad_pt_clean %>%
  group_by(plot_ID, subplot_ID) %>%
  summarise(
    area_ha = as.numeric(sf::st_area(sf::st_polygon(list(
      rbind(cbind(x_proj, y_proj), cbind(x_proj, y_proj)[1, ]))))) / 10000,
    .groups = "drop")

# Location of trees where no stems have coordinates, as bounds in the 
# relative coordinate system of the plot, from, in order of preference:
#   1. the bounds of the field subplot of the tree, in the optional subplot 
#        table
#   2. the extent of the stems with coordinates in the same field subplot, if
#        there are at least `subplot_min_stem` of them, within the plot
#   3. the extent of the plot corners
subplot_min_stem <- 10
plot_ext <- L0$pt %>%
  filter(corner %in% TRUE, !is.na(x_rel_m), !is.na(y_rel_m)) %>%
  group_by(plot_id) %>%
  summarise(
    px_min = min(x_rel_m), px_max = max(x_rel_m),
    py_min = min(y_rel_m), py_max = max(y_rel_m),
    .groups = "drop")
sub_ext <- L0$stem %>%
  filter(!is.na(subplot_id), subplot_id != "", !is.na(x_rel_m), !is.na(y_rel_m)) %>%
  group_by(plot_id, subplot_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_stem_mapped = n(),
    sx_min = min(x_rel_m), sx_max = max(x_rel_m),
    sy_min = min(y_rel_m), sy_max = max(y_rel_m),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_stem_mapped >= subplot_min_stem)
if (!is.null(L0$subplot)) {
  sub_tab <- dplyr::select(L0$subplot, plot_id, subplot_id,
    tx_min = x_rel_min_m, tx_max = x_rel_max_m, 
    ty_min = y_rel_min_m, ty_max = y_rel_max_m)
} else {
  sub_tab <- data.frame(plot_id = character(0), subplot_id = character(0),
    tx_min = numeric(0), tx_max = numeric(0), 
    ty_min = numeric(0), ty_max = numeric(0))
}

# One row per tree where no stems have coordinates, with the field subplot
# of its first stem with a subplot, and the sum of the simulated AGB of its 
# stems
tree_un <- stem_fil %>%
  mutate(row = row_number()) %>%
  filter(unmapped, in_agbd) %>%
  group_by(plot_id, tree_id, tree_key) %>%
  summarise(
    stem_id = paste(stem_id, collapse = ", "),
    n_stem = n(),
    subplot_id = first(na.omit(na_if(subplot_id, ""))),
    diam_eq_cm = first(diam_eq_cm),
    rows = list(row),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(., sub_tab, by = c("plot_id", "subplot_id")) %>%
  left_join(., sub_ext, by = c("plot_id", "subplot_id")) %>%
  left_join(., plot_ext, by = "plot_id") %>%
  mutate(
    location = case_when(
      !is.na(tx_min) ~ "field subplot, from subplot table",
      !is.na(sx_min) ~ "field subplot, from stems with coordinates",
      TRUE ~ "plot"),
    x_min = case_when(!is.na(tx_min) ~ tx_min, !is.na(sx_min) ~ pmax(sx_min, px_min), TRUE ~ px_min),
    x_max = case_when(!is.na(tx_max) ~ tx_max, !is.na(sx_max) ~ pmin(sx_max, px_max), TRUE ~ px_max),
    y_min = case_when(!is.na(ty_min) ~ ty_min, !is.na(sy_min) ~ pmax(sy_min, py_min), TRUE ~ py_min),
    y_max = case_when(!is.na(ty_max) ~ ty_max, !is.na(sy_max) ~ pmin(sy_max, py_max), TRUE ~ py_max))
tree_un_simu <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tree_un$rows, function(r) {
  colSums(agb_simu[r, , drop = FALSE])
}))
if (is.null(tree_un_simu)) {
  tree_un_simu <- matrix(numeric(0), nrow = 0, ncol = nsim)
}
tree_un$agb_Mg_mean <- rowMeans(tree_un_simu, na.rm = TRUE)

# Aggregate simulations to quadrats, separately for each plot
# Plots with no stems used to estimate AGB, e.g. plots with no trees above
# the minimum diameter threshold, have quadrats with zero AGB density
# Trees without coordinates are placed at random within their bounds in each
# simulation, see `tree_bounds` in BIOMASS::subplot_summary()
plot_vec <- unique(quad_pt_clean$plot_ID)
bound_cols <- c("x_min", "x_max", "y_min", "y_max")

quad_agb_simu <- bind_rows(lapply(plot_vec, function(x) {
  quads <- quad_area[quad_area$plot_ID == x, ]

  # Stems with coordinates, and trees without coordinates
  sel <- stem_fil$plot_id == x & !unmapped & in_agbd
  sel_un <- if (param$unmapped_method == "random") which(tree_un$plot_id == x) else integer(0)
  if (any(sel) || length(sel_un) > 0) {
    tree_data <- data.frame(
      plot_ID = x,
      subplot_ID = c(stem_fil$quadrat_id[sel], rep(NA_character_, length(sel_un))))
    tree_data[bound_cols] <- rbind(
      matrix(NA_real_, nrow = sum(sel), ncol = 4),
      as.matrix(tree_un[sel_un, bound_cols]))
    subplots <- list(
      sub_corner_coord = quad_pt_clean[quad_pt_clean$plot_ID == x, ],
      tree_data = tree_data)

    ss <- suppressMessages(BIOMASS::subplot_summary(
      subplots = subplots,
      AGB_simu = rbind(agb_simu[sel, , drop = FALSE], tree_un_simu[sel_un, , drop = FALSE]),
      draw_plot = FALSE,
      tree_bounds = if (length(sel_un) > 0) bound_cols else NULL))

    out <- as.data.frame(ss$long_AGB_simu) %>%
      dplyr::select(
        quadrat_id = subplot_ID,
        sim = N_simu,
        agbd_Mg_ha = AGBD)
  } else {
    out <- expand.grid(quadrat_id = quads$subplot_ID, sim = seq_len(nsim),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    out$agbd_Mg_ha <- 0
  }

  out$plot_id <- x
  out
}))
```

Trees without coordinates are written to `report/tree_unmapped.csv` by the
automated workflow, with the bounds they are placed within, and where the
bounds come from (`location`). We summarise them by location, and by field
subplot, as AGB per hectare of the subplot, to compare with quadrat AGB
density.

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Trees without coordinates, by where they are placed at random. pct_agb is the percentage of the AGB of all stems used to estimate AGB."
tree_unmapped <- tree_un %>%
  dplyr::select(plot_id, tree_id, stem_id, n_stem, diam_eq_cm, agb_Mg_mean,
    subplot_id, location, x_min, x_max, y_min, y_max)

kable(tree_un %>% 
  group_by(location) %>%
  summarise(n_tree = n(), agb_Mg = sum(agb_Mg_mean, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(pct_agb = round(100 * agb_Mg / sum(stem_agb_mc$agb_Mg_mean, na.rm = TRUE), 2)),
  digits = 3)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Simulated mean AGB of trees without coordinates in each field subplot, per hectare of the subplot, labelled with the number of trees. These trees are placed at random within their subplot in each simulation. Subplots without labels have no trees without coordinates. Trees without a field subplot are not shown."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
# Summarise trees without coordinates in each field subplot from the subplot
# table, as AGB per hectare of the subplot, to compare with quadrat AGB
# density
tree_un_sub <- filter(tree_un, location == "field subplot, from subplot table")
if (!is.null(L0$subplot) && nrow(tree_un_sub) > 0) {
  sub_un <- L0$subplot %>%
    mutate(plot_id = as.character(plot_id)) %>%
    filter(plot_id %in% tree_un_sub$plot_id) %>%
    left_join(., tree_un_sub %>%
      group_by(plot_id, subplot_id) %>%
      summarise(n_tree = n(), agb_Mg = sum(agb_Mg_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"),
      by = c("plot_id", "subplot_id")) %>%
    mutate(
      n_tree = ifelse(is.na(n_tree), 0L, n_tree),
      agb_Mg = ifelse(is.na(agb_Mg), 0, agb_Mg),
      area_ha = (x_rel_max_m - x_rel_min_m) * (y_rel_max_m - y_rel_min_m) / 10000,
      agbd_Mg_ha = agb_Mg / area_ha,
      x_mid = (x_rel_min_m + x_rel_max_m) / 2,
      y_mid = (y_rel_min_m + y_rel_max_m) / 2)

  # Figure of the AGB of trees without coordinates in each field subplot.
  # Labels are light on the darkest fills
  n_plot_un <- length(unique(sub_un$plot_id))
  un_lim <- c(0, max(c(sub_un$agbd_Mg_ha, 1e-6)))
  sub_un$label_colour <- ifelse(sub_un$agbd_Mg_ha < 0.6 * un_lim[2],
    fig_pal$ink, fig_pal$surface)
  p_sub_un <- ggplot(sub_un) +
    geom_blank(data = squareExtent(
      data.frame(plot_id = rep(sub_un$plot_id, 2),
        x = c(sub_un$x_rel_min_m, sub_un$x_rel_max_m),
        y = c(sub_un$y_rel_min_m, sub_un$y_rel_max_m)), "x", "y", "plot_id"),
      aes(x = x, y = y)) +
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = x_rel_min_m, xmax = x_rel_max_m, ymin = y_rel_min_m,
      ymax = y_rel_max_m, fill = agbd_Mg_ha),
      colour = fig_pal$surface, linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_gradientn("AGB of trees without coordinates (Mg/ha)",
      colours = fig_pal$seq2, limits = un_lim, guide = colourBar()) +
    geom_text(data = filter(sub_un, n_tree > 0),
      aes(x = x_mid, y = y_mid, label = n_tree, colour = label_colour),
      size = 3.2) +
    scale_colour_identity() +
    facet_wrap(vars(plotFactor(plot_id)), ncol = figCols(n_plot_un),
      scales = "free") +
    labs(
      title = "Trees without coordinates in each field subplot",
      x = "X (m)",
      y = "Y (m)") +
    themeMap() +
    theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
  print(p_sub_un)
}

```

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Field subplots with the most AGB in trees without coordinates (Mg/ha of the subplot)."
#| eval: !expr exists("sub_un")
kable(head(sub_un %>%
  filter(n_tree > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(agbd_Mg_ha)) %>%
  transmute(plot_id, subplot_id, n_tree, agb_Mg, area_ha, agbd_Mg_ha), 10), digits = 3)
```

Assigning all of a tree's AGB to the quadrat containing its stems ignores
that the crowns of large trees often spread into neighbouring quadrats,
which is what airborne lidar sees. Optionally (`crown_method: "custom"`),
quadrat AGBD is also estimated with the AGB of each tree spread over its
crown, a circle centred on the tree with area from the crown area allometry
in `crown_custom`. The residual error of the allometry is drawn
independently for each tree in each simulation. Crowns inside their home
quadrat are assigned to it, and crowns crossing a quadrat edge are split
among quadrats by the share of 512 points spread evenly over the crown in
each quadrat, see `crownAlloc()` in `func.R`. The part of a crown outside
the quadrat grid is folded back into the part inside, so plot AGBD is
unchanged, and only its distribution among quadrats changes. Trees without
coordinates, placed at random, and trees with an imputed diameter keep stem
allocation. Crown area is predicted from the measured diameter, the
equivalent diameter of the measured diameters of multi-stemmed trees, not
corrected for taper, as crown allometries are fitted to measured diameters.
It is not predicted from the simulated diameter, as `AGBmonteCarlo()` does
not return simulated diameters. The example data use the default, `"none"`, so here we use the
crown area allometry of @MartinezCano2019 for Barro Colorado Island to
illustrate, without adding it to the results:

```{r}
# Crown area allometry, see `crown_custom` in param.yaml
crown_custom <- if (!is.null(param$crown_custom)) {
  param$crown_custom
} else {
  list(
    formula = "a * D^b",
    parameters = list(a = 0.57, b = 1.34),
    sigma = 0.549,
    link = "log",
    reference = "Martinez-Cano et al. (2019)")
}
crown_mod <- crownCustom(crown_custom)
crown_tmpl <- crownTemplate(n_ring = 16, n_angle = 32)
quad_rel <- st_drop_geometry(quad_pt)

# Stems without coordinates in trees where other stems have coordinates are
# given the mean coordinates of the other stems of the tree, as in [Fit plot
# spatial polygons], where trees are assigned to quadrats
xy_fill <- L0$stem %>%
  mutate(tree_grp = ifelse(is.na(tree_id) | tree_id == "",
    paste0("record::", record_id), paste(plot_id, tree_id, sep = "::"))) %>%
  group_by(tree_grp) %>%
  mutate(
    xy_ok = !is.na(x_rel_m) & !is.na(y_rel_m),
    x_rel_m = ifelse(!xy_ok & any(xy_ok), mean(x_rel_m[xy_ok]), x_rel_m),
    y_rel_m = ifelse(!xy_ok & any(xy_ok), mean(y_rel_m[xy_ok]), y_rel_m)) %>%
  ungroup()
xy_i <- match(stem_fil$record_id, xy_fill$record_id)

# Difference in AGB density of each quadrat between crown and stem
# allocation, in each simulation, and trees with a crown
crown_list <- lapply(plot_vec, function(x) {
  grid <- quadGrid(quad_rel[quad_rel$plot_id == x, ])
  # Stems with coordinates in a quadrat, as in the stem allocation above
  rows <- which(stem_fil$plot_id == x & !unmapped & in_agbd &
    !is.na(stem_fil$quadrat_id))
  if (is.null(grid) || length(rows) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # One row per tree, at the centroid of its stems, with the equivalent
  # diameter of the measured diameters of its stems
  s <- stem_fil[rows, ]
  s$x_rel_m <- xy_fill$x_rel_m[xy_i[rows]]
  s$y_rel_m <- xy_fill$y_rel_m[xy_i[rows]]
  tr <- s %>%
    group_by(tree_key) %>%
    summarise(
      x = mean(x_rel_m, na.rm = TRUE),
      y = mean(y_rel_m, na.rm = TRUE),
      quadrat_id = first(quadrat_id),
      diam_crown_cm = sqrt(sum(diam_cm_meas^2)),
      .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(home = match(quadrat_id, grid$quad$quadrat_id))
  agb_s <- agb_simu[rows, , drop = FALSE]
  agb_s[is.na(agb_s)] <- 0
  agb_t <- rowsum(agb_s, s$tree_key)[tr$tree_key, , drop = FALSE]

  # Trees with an imputed diameter keep stem allocation, as a crown of
  # radius 0 at the centre of the home quadrat
  has_crown <- is.finite(tr$diam_crown_cm) & is.finite(tr$x) & is.finite(tr$y)
  hq <- grid$quad[tr$home, ]
  tr$x[!has_crown] <- (hq$x_min[!has_crown] + hq$x_max[!has_crown]) / 2
  tr$y[!has_crown] <- (hq$y_min[!has_crown] + hq$y_max[!has_crown]) / 2

  nq <- nrow(grid$quad)
  delta <- vapply(seq_len(nsim), function(j) {
    r <- numeric(nrow(tr))
    r[has_crown] <- sqrt(crownArea(crown_mod, tr$diam_crown_cm[has_crown],
      rnorm(sum(has_crown))) / pi)
    crown_q <- crownAlloc(tr$x, tr$y, agb_t[, j], r, tr$home, grid, crown_tmpl)
    stem_q <- numeric(nq)
    s_q <- rowsum(agb_t[, j], tr$home)
    stem_q[as.integer(rownames(s_q))] <- s_q[, 1]
    crown_q - stem_q
  }, numeric(nq))

  quads <- quad_area[quad_area$plot_ID == x, ]
  area_ha <- quads$area_ha[match(grid$quad$quadrat_id, quads$subplot_ID)]
  list(
    tree = data.frame(
      plot_id = x,
      x = tr$x[has_crown],
      y = tr$y[has_crown],
      r = sqrt(crownArea(crown_mod, tr$diam_crown_cm[has_crown]) / pi),
      agb_Mg = rowMeans(agb_t[has_crown, , drop = FALSE])),
    delta = data.frame(
      plot_id = x,
      quadrat_id = rep(grid$quad$quadrat_id, nsim),
      sim = rep(seq_len(nsim), each = nq),
      agbd_diff = as.vector(delta / area_ha)))
})
crown_list <- Filter(Negate(is.null), crown_list)
crown_delta <- bind_rows(lapply(crown_list, `[[`, "delta"))

# Add crown-distributed AGB density to the simulations, if `crown_method`
# is "custom"
if (param$crown_method != "none") {
  quad_agb_simu <- quad_agb_simu %>%
    left_join(., crown_delta, by = c("plot_id", "quadrat_id", "sim")) %>%
    mutate(agbd_Mg_ha_crown = agbd_Mg_ha + coalesce(agbd_diff, 0)) %>%
    dplyr::select(-agbd_diff)
}
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Quadrat AGB density with tree AGB spread over crowns, minus quadrat AGB density with each tree in its home quadrat, simulated means."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
# Figure of the difference in quadrat AGB density between crown and stem
# allocation, simulated means
crown_fig <- quad_rel %>%
  group_by(plot_id, quadrat_id) %>%
  summarise(
    x_min = min(x_rel_m), x_max = max(x_rel_m),
    y_min = min(y_rel_m), y_max = max(y_rel_m),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  inner_join(., crown_delta %>%
    group_by(plot_id, quadrat_id) %>%
    summarise(agbd_diff = mean(agbd_diff), .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("plot_id", "quadrat_id"))
n_plot_crown <- length(unique(crown_fig$plot_id))
diff_lim <- c(-1, 1) * max(abs(crown_fig$agbd_diff), 1e-6)
ggplot(crown_fig) +
  geom_blank(data = squareExtent(
    data.frame(plot_id = rep(crown_fig$plot_id, 2),
      x = c(crown_fig$x_min, crown_fig$x_max),
      y = c(crown_fig$y_min, crown_fig$y_max)), "x", "y", "plot_id"),
    aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = x_min, xmax = x_max, ymin = y_min, ymax = y_max,
    fill = agbd_diff), colour = fig_pal$surface, linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2("Crown minus stem allocation (Mg/ha)",
    low = fig_pal$series[1], mid = fig_pal$surface, high = fig_pal$series[2],
    midpoint = 0, limits = diff_lim, guide = colourBar()) +
  facet_wrap(vars(plotFactor(plot_id)), ncol = figCols(n_plot_crown),
    scales = "free") +
  labs(
    title = "Quadrat AGBD, crown minus stem allocation",
    x = "X (m)",
    y = "Y (m)") +
  themeMap() +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Tree crowns in each plot, as translucent circles with the median crown area from the crown area allometry, filled by the simulated mean AGB of the tree, with quadrats."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
# Figure of tree crowns in each plot, as circles with the median crown area,
# filled by the simulated mean AGB of the tree. Larger crowns are drawn
# first, so smaller crowns stay visible
crown_tree <- bind_rows(lapply(crown_list, `[[`, "tree")) %>%
  filter(agb_Mg > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(r)) %>%
  mutate(tree = row_number())
circ_n <- 24
circ_a <- 2 * pi * seq_len(circ_n) / circ_n
crown_poly <- data.frame(
  plot_id = rep(crown_tree$plot_id, each = circ_n),
  tree = rep(crown_tree$tree, each = circ_n),
  agb_Mg = rep(crown_tree$agb_Mg, each = circ_n),
  x = rep(crown_tree$x, each = circ_n) +
    as.vector(outer(cos(circ_a), crown_tree$r)),
  y = rep(crown_tree$y, each = circ_n) +
    as.vector(outer(sin(circ_a), crown_tree$r)))
ggplot() +
  geom_blank(data = squareExtent(
    data.frame(plot_id = rep(crown_fig$plot_id, 2),
      x = c(crown_fig$x_min, crown_fig$x_max),
      y = c(crown_fig$y_min, crown_fig$y_max)), "x", "y", "plot_id"),
    aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_polygon(data = crown_poly, aes(x = x, y = y, group = tree,
    fill = agb_Mg), alpha = 0.4, colour = NA) +
  geom_rect(data = crown_fig, aes(xmin = x_min, xmax = x_max,
    ymin = y_min, ymax = y_max), fill = NA, colour = fig_pal$ink_muted,
    linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_gradientn("Tree AGB (Mg)", colours = fig_pal$seq2[-1],
    trans = "log10", breaks = 10^(-3:3),
    labels = function(x) format(x, drop0trailing = TRUE,
      scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE),
    guide = colourBar()) +
  facet_wrap(vars(plotFactor(plot_id)), ncol = figCols(n_plot_crown),
    scales = "free") +
  labs(
    title = "Tree crowns in each plot",
    x = "X (m)",
    y = "Y (m)") +
  themeMap() +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
```

Finally extract relevant summary statistics from the AGBD error propagation:

```{r}
# Extract summary statistics from AGBD simulations. With crown allocation,
# also `agbd_Mg_ha_crown_mc_*`
quad_agb <- quad_agb_simu %>%
  group_by(plot_id, quadrat_id) %>%
  summarise(
    agbd_Mg_ha_mc_mean = mean(agbd_Mg_ha),
    agbd_Mg_ha_mc_median = median(agbd_Mg_ha),
    agbd_Mg_ha_mc_sd = sd(agbd_Mg_ha),
    agbd_Mg_ha_mc_ci2.5 = quantile(agbd_Mg_ha, 0.025),
    agbd_Mg_ha_mc_ci97.5 = quantile(agbd_Mg_ha, 0.975),
    across(any_of("agbd_Mg_ha_crown"), list(
      mc_mean = mean,
      mc_median = median,
      mc_sd = sd,
      mc_ci2.5 = ~quantile(.x, 0.025),
      mc_ci97.5 = ~quantile(.x, 0.975))),
    .groups = "drop")
```

We summarise plot-level AGB density and its uncertainty, from the
area-weighted mean of quadrat AGB density in each simulation. This is
compared to the sum of stem AGB from [Estimate stem AGB] over the same area.
The two should be similar. Differences arise from stems excluded from
quadrats, from trees without coordinates or diameters, and because
measurement errors are not symmetric on the AGB scale.

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Plot AGB density (Mg/ha) over the quadrat grid, from the simulations (mc), and the sum of stem AGB (stem_sum). diff_pct is the difference between them."
# Summarise plot-level AGB density and its uncertainty, from the area-weighted
# mean of quadrat AGB density in each simulation. This is compared to the sum
# of stem AGB from ./05_agb_stem.R over the same area. The two should be 
# similar. Differences arise from stems excluded from quadrats, and because
# measurement errors are not symmetric on the AGB scale
quad_area_join <- quad_area %>%
  transmute(plot_id = as.character(plot_ID), quadrat_id = subplot_ID, area_ha)

plot_agb_mc <- quad_agb_simu %>%
  mutate(plot_id = as.character(plot_id)) %>%
  inner_join(., quad_area_join, by = c("plot_id", "quadrat_id")) %>%
  group_by(plot_id, sim) %>%
  summarise(agbd_Mg_ha = sum(agbd_Mg_ha * area_ha) / sum(area_ha), 
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(plot_id) %>%
  summarise(
    agbd_Mg_ha_mc_mean = mean(agbd_Mg_ha),
    agbd_Mg_ha_mc_sd = sd(agbd_Mg_ha),
    agbd_Mg_ha_mc_ci2.5 = quantile(agbd_Mg_ha, 0.025),
    agbd_Mg_ha_mc_ci97.5 = quantile(agbd_Mg_ha, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop")

# Stems in strips of the plot left out of the quadrat grid are excluded, as
# the quadrat grid area does not include them
plot_agb_det <- stem_fil %>%
  filter(as.character(record_id) %in% record_agbd, !grid_excl) %>%
  dplyr::select(record_id, plot_id) %>%
  inner_join(., stem_agb_all, by = "record_id") %>%
  mutate(plot_id = as.character(plot_id)) %>%
  group_by(plot_id) %>%
  summarise(agb_Mg = sum(agb_Mg, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  right_join(., quad_area_join %>% group_by(plot_id) %>% 
    summarise(area_ha = sum(area_ha), n_quadrat = n(), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "plot_id") %>%
  mutate(
    agb_Mg = ifelse(is.na(agb_Mg), 0, agb_Mg),
    agbd_Mg_ha_stem_sum = agb_Mg / area_ha)

plot_agb_check <- plot_agb_det %>%
  dplyr::select(plot_id, n_quadrat, area_ha, agbd_Mg_ha_stem_sum) %>%
  inner_join(., plot_agb_mc, by = "plot_id") %>%
  mutate(
    # Undefined for plots with zero AGB density
    cv_pct = ifelse(agbd_Mg_ha_mc_mean > 0, 
      round(100 * agbd_Mg_ha_mc_sd / agbd_Mg_ha_mc_mean, 1), NA_real_),
    diff_pct = ifelse(agbd_Mg_ha_stem_sum > 0, 
      round(100 * (agbd_Mg_ha_mc_mean - agbd_Mg_ha_stem_sum) / 
        agbd_Mg_ha_stem_sum, 1), NA_real_)) %>%
  arrange(desc(agbd_Mg_ha_mc_mean))

if (any(abs(plot_agb_check$diff_pct) > 10, na.rm = TRUE)) {
  warning("Simulated plot AGB density differs from the sum of stem AGB by ",
    "more than 10% in plots: ", 
    paste(plot_agb_check$plot_id[abs(plot_agb_check$diff_pct) > 10], collapse = ", "),
    ". Check stems outside the quadrat grid, see ", 
    file.path(report_dir, "stem_outside.csv"), call. = FALSE)
}

kable(plot_agb_check)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Plot AGB density over the quadrat grid of each plot, from error propagation (simulated mean with 95% interval), and from the sum of stem AGB."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
# Figure of plot AGB density with 95% interval from simulations, and the 
# sum of stem AGB
plot_agb_fig <- plot_agb_check %>%
  mutate(plot_id = factor(plot_id, levels = rev(levels(plotFactor(plot_id)))))
p_plot_agb <- ggplot(plot_agb_fig, aes(y = plot_id)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = agbd_Mg_ha_mc_ci2.5, xmax = agbd_Mg_ha_mc_ci97.5),
    colour = fig_pal$series[1], linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(x = agbd_Mg_ha_mc_mean, shape = "Simulated mean, 95% interval"),
    colour = fig_pal$series[1], size = 2.4) +
  geom_point(aes(x = agbd_Mg_ha_stem_sum, shape = "Sum of stem AGB"),
    colour = fig_pal$ink, size = 2.4, stroke = 0.7) +
  scale_shape_manual(NULL, values = c("Simulated mean, 95% interval" = 16, 
    "Sum of stem AGB" = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Plot AGBD",
    x = "AGBD (Mg/ha)",
    y = "Plot") +
  themeFig()
p_plot_agb
```

#| fig-cap: "Distribution of Monte-Carlo simulations of above-ground woody biomass density (AGBD) for the top 10 quadrats with the highest AGBD."

quadrat_agb_top <- quad_agb %>%

# Visualise Monte-Carlo AGBD simulations for each of the top 10 quadrats with the highest AGBD

## Compile GEO-TREES L1, L2, and L3 data products 

`09_stem_summ.R`
`10_quad_summ.R`
`11_brm.R`

Now we have everything needed to create the GEO-TREES L1, L2 and L3 data products.

First we create a master stem table containing all the calculated values from
the previous steps. This table contains many more columns than will be in the
official GEO-TREES data products.

```{r}
# Combine stem dataframes
# Stems without coordinates have empty point geometries
stem_summ <- L0$stem %>%
  left_join(., stem_taxa_all, by = c("taxon_name" = "nameOriginal")) %>%
  left_join(., stem_wd_all, by = "record_id") %>%
  left_join(., stem_height_all, by = "record_id") %>%
  left_join(., stem_agb_all, by = "record_id") %>%
  left_join(., stem_agb_mc, by = "record_id") %>%
  left_join(., st_drop_geometry(stem_pt), by = "record_id") %>%
  mutate(
    # Stems without coordinates in trees with other stems that have 
    # coordinates take the quadrat of the tree
    quadrat_id = coalesce(quadrat_id_tree, quadrat_id),
    # Used to estimate AGB, and AGB density. Stems outside the quadrat grid
    # are not used to estimate AGB density
    in_agb_calc = record_id %in% record_fil,
    in_quadrat_calc = in_quadrat_calc %in% TRUE,
    # Diameter imputed, and coordinates from the mean of the other stems of 
    # the tree
    diam_imputed = diam_imputed %in% TRUE,
    xy_from_tree = xy_from_tree %in% TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::select(-quadrat_id_tree) %>%
  st_as_sf(., coords = c("x_utm", "y_utm"), crs = st_crs(stem_pt),
    na.fail = FALSE, remove = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| tab-cap: "Example of master stems table."
# Inspect master stem table
kable(head(stem_summ, 10))
```

Similarly, we create a master quadrat table, with many calculated values, more
than will be in the official GEO-TREES data products.

```{r}
# Calculate area of each quadrat
quad_poly$plot_id <- as.character(quad_poly$plot_id)
quad_poly_area <- st_drop_geometry(quad_poly)
quad_poly_area$quadrat_area_ha <- as.vector(st_area(quad_poly)) * 0.0001
quad_poly_area$quadrat_dim_x_m <- param$quad_dim[1]
quad_poly_area$quadrat_dim_y_m <- param$quad_dim[2]

# Calculate quadrat summary values
quad_summ_pre <- stem_summ %>% 
  filter(in_quadrat_calc == TRUE) %>% 
  st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  group_by(site_id, acquisition_id, plot_id, quadrat_id) %>% 
  summarise(
    census_date = median(measurement_date, na.rm = TRUE),
    census_date_res = case_when(
      any(measurement_date_res == "YYYY") ~ "YYYY",
      any(measurement_date_res == "YYYY-MM") ~ "YYYY-MM",
      any(measurement_date_res == "YYYY-MM-DD") ~ "YYYY-MM-DD",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_),
    n_stem = n(),
    agb_Mg_sum = sum(agb_Mg, na.rm = TRUE),
    ba_m2_sum = sum(ba_m2, na.rm = TRUE),
    volume_m3_sum = sum(volume_m3, na.rm = TRUE),
    diam_cm_mean = mean(diam_cm, na.rm = TRUE),
    diam_cm_max = max(diam_cm, na.rm = TRUE),
    diam_cm_q80 = quantile(diam_cm, 0.8, na.rm = TRUE),
    diam_cm_q90 = quantile(diam_cm, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE),
    diam_cm_q95 = quantile(diam_cm, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
    height_m_pred_mean = mean(height_m_pred, na.rm = TRUE),
    height_m_pred_max_rse = height_m_pred_rse[which(height_m_pred == max(height_m_pred, na.rm = TRUE))][1],
    height_m_pred_max = max(height_m_pred, na.rm = TRUE),
    height_m_pred_q80 = quantile(height_m_pred, 0.8, na.rm = TRUE),
    height_m_pred_q90 = quantile(height_m_pred, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE),
    height_m_pred_q95 = quantile(height_m_pred, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
    lorey_height_m = sum(ba_m2 * height_m_pred, na.rm = TRUE) / 
      sum(ba_m2[!is.na(height_m_pred)], na.rm = TRUE),
    meanWD_mean = mean(meanWD, na.rm = TRUE),
    meanWD_wm_ba = weighted.mean(meanWD, ba_m2, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop_last") %>% 
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      .cols = where(~inherits(.x, "units")), 
      .fns = as.vector),
    # max() of only NAs returns -Inf
    across(
      .cols = where(is.numeric), 
      .fns = ~replace(.x, is.infinite(.x), NA_real_))) 
  
# Add quadrat polygons, fill in quadrats with no trees
quad_summ <- quad_poly %>% 
  left_join(., quad_poly_area, 
    by = c("site_id", "acquisition_id", "plot_id", "quadrat_id")) %>% 
  left_join(., quad_summ_pre, 
    by = c("site_id", "acquisition_id", "plot_id", "quadrat_id")) %>% 
  # Quadrat AGBD from error propagation, including stems without coordinates
  left_join(., quad_agb, by = c("plot_id", "quadrat_id")) %>%
  mutate(
    empty_quadrat = is.na(n_stem),
    across(
      c(
        any_of(c(
          "n_stem", 
          "ba_m2_sum",
          "volume_m3_sum",
          "agb_Mg_sum")),
        starts_with(c("agbd_Mg_ha_mc_", "agbd_Mg_ha_crown_mc_"))), 
      ~if_else(empty_quadrat & is.na(.x), 0, .x)),
    across(
      c(
        all_of("n_stem"),
        starts_with(c("ba_m2_", "volume_m3_", "agb_Mg"))),
      ~.x / quadrat_area_ha,
      .names = "{.col}_ha")) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-empty_quadrat)
```
